papers.abstract: Intravenous lipid emulsion (ILE) is the recommended first-line treatment for local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST), particularly when cardiovascular compromise occurs. However, uncertainty persists regarding the optimal lipid formulation, specifically the comparative efficacy of ILEs containing 100% long-chain triglycerides (LCT) versus ILEs containing a 50/50 mixture of medium- and long-chain triglycerides (MCT/LCT), as well as ILEs with a 20% versus 30% lipid concentration. The primary aim of this narrative review was to compare the efficacy of 100% LCT-containing ILEs versus 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs by analyzing their respective mechanisms of action in experimental models of local anesthetic-induced cardiovascular toxicity, whereas the secondary objective was to compare ILEs with a 20% versus a 30% lipid concentration. The review also integrates the physiological rationale underlying lipid resuscitation and explores a mechanistically informed framework for interpreting formulation-specific effects of ILEs. A literature search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar was conducted from January 1998 through January 2026. Twenty experimental studies were identified-nine in vitro, one ex vivo, and ten in vivo-and qualitatively synthesized according to their principal mechanisms of action, including lipid shuttle, cardiotonic, vascular, and metabolic effects. The available experimental evidence suggests that 100% LCT-containing ILEs provide greater overall cardiovascular recovery than 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs, particularly through more effective lipid-shuttle activity and sustained myocardial protection. Conversely, 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs demonstrated greater vascular effects in several experimental models. Evidence comparing lipid concentrations was limited to 100% LCT-containing formulations and generally showed greater pharmacokinetic, hemodynamic, and survival effects with a 30% versus a 20% lipid concentration when administered at the same volume. The available evidence is derived exclusively from heterogeneous preclinical experimental models and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than practice-informing. Triglyceride composition and lipid concentration may influence distinct mechanisms contributing to cardiovascular recovery during LAST. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for exploring formulation-phenotype associations but do not establish formulation-specific treatment recommendations. Further experimental and translational studies are needed to determine whether these mechanistic findings translate into clinically meaningful benefits in patients with LAST.

papers.abstract: Severe neurologic injury after uncomplicated general anesthesia in previously healthy patients is rare. Since 2021, reports from South America and later from North America and Europe have described catastrophic neurologic deterioration and death after routine general anesthesia in children and adults with Venezuelan maternal ancestry. A homoplasmic mitochondrial DNA variant, MT-ND4 m.11232 T > C (p.Leu158Pro), affecting complex I of the electron transport chain, has emerged as the leading candidate susceptibility factor. This systematic review identified, appraised, and synthesized available evidence linking inhaled anesthetics, in particular sevoflurane, with severe perioperative neurologic complications in carriers of this variant and in individuals with Venezuelan maternal ancestry. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261471143), with searches of major biomedical databases, gray literature, and variant databases. The evidence describes a consistent but incompletely characterized syndrome defined by maternal Venezuelan ancestry, apparent preoperative health, predominant sevoflurane exposure, delayed emergence, and severe basal ganglia injury with frequent death. In patient-derived fibroblasts and cybrids, sevoflurane markedly suppressed complex I-dependent respiration, whereas propofol did not. Incidence, penetrance, and agent-specific risk remain uncertain. Cautious perioperative strategies that avoid volatile anesthetics appear justified.

papers.abstract: Lateral cavernous-sinus extension and suprasellar tumor-arachnoid anatomy are distinct but overlapping dimensions of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET) surgery. We evaluated whether reader-concordant preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) descriptors of these two axes show different associations with extent of resection and intraoperative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leakage. In this single-center retrospective study, two blinded neurosurgeons independently assessed preoperative MRI of 53 patients: modified Knosp grade, suprasellar height, bowing index, infundibular deviation angle, and a study-specific tumor-arachnoid cleft grade. Exploratory analyses examined resection extent and Esposito-graded leakage (15 events), with post hoc adjustment for maximal tumor diameter. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were 0.995-0.999 for continuous measures; cleft agreement was 53/53 and Knosp exact agreement 96.2%. Knosp grade was most strongly associated with non-total resection (area under the curve [AUC] 0.908; diameter-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 10.8 per SD, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.4-48.9) but not leakage (AUC 0.648). Suprasellar height (AUC 0.747) and cleft grade (AUC 0.740) showed stronger leakage associations; none of 16 patients with a wide cleft (> 2 mm) leaked. Cleft grade and height were strongly collinear (ρ=-0.81); the cleft-leakage association persisted after diameter adjustment (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.19-0.93). Lateral and suprasellar MRI descriptors, concordant between two readers, showed different, partly overlapping operative associations. Modified Knosp grade related most strongly to resection, whereas suprasellar features, particularly the study-specific cleft grade, showed stronger exploratory associations with intraoperative leakage. The cleft finding is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective external validation; added value over height and the sellar barrier is unproven.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma frequently progresses beyond surgical margins, yet whether preoperative imaging can predict its direction remains unclear. Given the anatomical characteristics of the temporal lobe and the potential role of anterior temporal lobectomy, we evaluated FLAIR, isotropic diffusion (DTI-p), and diffusion anisotropy (DTI-q) as imaging biomarkers of directional progression after complete resection. We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively recruited multicenter cohort of patients with newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype glioblastoma confined to the temporal lobe who underwent complete resection of contrast-enhancing tumor and had preoperative diffusion tensor imaging and follow-up MRI demonstrating progression. Progression was visually classified relative to the resection cavity. Direction-specific accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were calculated, with paired comparisons using exact McNemar tests and Holm correction across all comparisons. Times to progression and death were summarized descriptively. Thirty-two patients met inclusion criteria. DTI-q demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy across all progression directions (median, 75%), compared with DTI-p (median, 50%) and FLAIR (median, 44%). DTI-q significantly outperformed FLAIR and DTI-p for lateral, superior, and inferior progression after Holm correction. Combined imaging models did not improve predictive performance over DTI-q alone. Preoperative DTI-q predicted directional progression after complete resection more accurately than FLAIR or DTI-p, supporting DTI-q as a potential imaging biomarker for spatially informed surgical planning.

papers.abstract: Robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC) is increasingly prevalent. However, real-world data on its mid-term effectiveness in diverse patient populations remain limited. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study of patients undergoing RARC for bladder cancer at 32 Chinese institutions (2012-2021). Baseline, perioperative, pathological, and survival data were collected. Missing data were handled by multiple imputation. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and cancer-specific survival (CSS). Multivariable Cox regression was used to identify independent prognostic factors. Among the 4395 enrolled patients, the median age was 65 years, and 85.1% were male. With a median follow-up of 26.6 months (interquartile range 12.7-47.6), the estimated 3-year OS, RFS, and CSS were 78.7%, 74.9%, and 81.7%, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified non-organ-confined disease (pT3-4) and lymph node metastasis as independent prognostic factors for worse OS, RFS, and CSS (all p<0.001). Adjuvant therapy was independently associated with worse RFS (hazard ratio 1.687; 95% confidence interval 1.389-2.049, p<0.001), and cutaneous ureterostomy was associated with worse RFS than ileal conduit (hazard ratio 1.241; 95% confidence interval 1.007-1.531, p=0.040). This large real-world study demonstrates that RARC provides satisfactory mid-term oncologic outcomes. Charlson Comorbidity Index, tumor stage, lymph node status, and urinary diversion choice significantly affect survival. These findings support the continued adoption of RARC and highlight the importance of patient selection and comprehensive perioperative management.

papers.abstract: Effective therapy remains lacking for patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) whose disease progressed after standard treatment. Izalontamab brengitecan, an epidermal growth factor receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor, Ed-04, has shown clinical activity in ESCC in a phase 1b study. To evaluate the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan compared with chemotherapy in patients with advanced ESCC who progressed after first-line programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy. This phase 3, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted across 80 hospitals in China. Patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC that had progressed with first-line PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy were enrolled. Between March 19, 2024, and August 1, 2025 (final follow-up, October 17, 2025), a total of 704 patients were screened, and 497 were enrolled and randomized. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either izalontamab brengitecan (n = 249; 2.5 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks) or physician-selected chemotherapy (n = 248; irinotecan, paclitaxel, or docetaxel) every 3 weeks. The dual primary end points were progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 and overall survival (OS). Of 497 patients who underwent randomization (median age, 61.0 years [range, 34-76]; 448 male patients [90.1%]), 493 received study treatment. At this interim analysis, izalontamab brengitecan demonstrated statistically significant improvement in both PFS and OS. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 4.17 months (95% CI, 3.61-4.53 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 1.97 months (95% CI, 1.61-2.73 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.40-0.63; log-rank P < .001). Median OS was 9.79 months (95% CI, 7.89-11.01 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 7.20 months (95% CI, 6.18-7.82 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48-0.82; log-rank P < .001). papers.abstract: Oral nutritional supplementation (ONS), providing supplementary oral nutrition in addition to usual food, is widely used during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but its optimal timing and cost utility remain uncertain. To evaluate efficacy and explore cost utility of early ONS in patients with NPC undergoing CCRT. This multicenter, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 6 Chinese tertiary hospitals from July 2021 to May 2025. Eligible patients were aged 18 to 70 years with newly diagnosed stage II to IVA NPC, a Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA) score of 0 to 8, and planned CCRT. Key exclusions included oral intake less than 60% of requirements for 3 days or longer, inability or unwillingness to receive concurrent chemotherapy, and inability to receive oral or enteral nutrition. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to March 2026. Participants were randomized 1:1 to early ONS at CCRT start or routine ONS after prespecified nutritional decline. The primary end point was the incidence of more than 5% weight loss from baseline to CCRT completion. Secondary end points included PG-SGA score, the incidence of grade 3 or higher radiation-induced oral mucositis (RIOM), quality of life (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30), and radiotherapy interruption. Cost utility measures included total cost, utility, and incremental cost utility ratio. Of 242 patients screened, 236 patients were randomized, and the prespecified modified intention-to-treat population included 216 patients (mean [SD] age, 46.62 [11.19] years; 168 [77.8%] male), with 107 receiving early ONS and 109 receiving routine ONS. More than 5% weight loss occurred in 70 participants (65.4% ) in the early ONS group, compared with 88 participants (80.7%) in the routine ONS group (relative risk [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.96; P = .01). An intention-to-treat analysis including all randomized participants yielded a similar estimate (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.65-0.93). In the modified intention-to-treat population, grade 3 or higher RIOM occurred in 15 participants (14.0%) in the early ONS group vs 29 participants (26.6%) in the routine ONS group (RR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.30-0.93). Best-case costs were $9560.56 in the early ONS group vs $9685.23 in the routine ONS group, with quality-adjusted life-years of 0.1144 vs 0.1132, respectively. This randomized clinical trial found that early ONS reduced clinically meaningful weight loss during CCRT; exploratory analyses suggested potential benefits for severe RIOM and a potentially favorable short-term economic profile. papers.abstract: Despite multimodal treatment, recurrence remains common in patients with resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Whether perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improves long-term outcomes remains uncertain. To estimate the effect of perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy on event-free survival (EFS) compared with standard surgery-based treatment in patients with resectable locally advanced HNSCC. The CAMORAL trial was a multicenter, phase 2 randomized clinical trial conducted at 4 academic hospitals in China between October 2020 and March 2024, with data cutoff on April 11, 2025. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with untreated, resectable stage III to IVB HNSCC were assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant treatment or control. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to February 2026. Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive two 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant camrelizumab, 200 mg, plus albumin-bound paclitaxel and carboplatin followed by surgery, risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, and maintenance camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles; or upfront surgery followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy. The primary end point was 2-year EFS. Secondary end points included major pathological response (MPR), pathological complete response (pCR), overall survival, 2-year distant metastasis-free survival, 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival, and safety. Of 125 included patients, 99 (79.2%) were male, and the mean (SD) age was 56.3 (11.7) years. A total of 63 patients were assigned to the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 62 to the control group; the median (IQR) follow-up was 24.6 (16.8-36.5) months. A total of 103 (82.4%) had oral cavity primary tumors. Among 125 patients, the 2-year EFS rate was 77.8% (95% CI, 63.6-87.0) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group compared with 46.1% (95% CI, 31.3-59.6) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). MPR and pCR were 47.6% (95% CI, 34.9-60.6) and 25.4% (95% CI, 15.3-37.9), respectively, in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group, with no MPR or pCR events in the control group. The 2-year overall survival rates were 92.0% and 69.1%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.10-0.64); the hazard ratio of 2-year distant metastasis-free survival was 0.15 (95% CI, 0.03-0.68). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50 of 63 patients (79.4%) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 35 of 62 patients (56.5%) in the control group; 1 fatal treatment-emergent adverse event occurred in the control group. In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved EFS with manageable toxic effects, supporting evaluation of intensified perioperative immune priming in resectable HNSCC. papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This retrospective study aimed to identify molecular predictors of treatment response and survival in 207 newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients treated with Venetoclax combined with hypomethylating agents (VEN‐HMAs). After one treatment course, the composite complete remission (CR/CRi) rate was 69.6% (144/207), with 70.5% (93/132) of responders achieving minimal residual disease (MRD) negativity. According to the 2017 ELN risk stratification, the CR/CRi rates in the favorable‐, intermediate‐, and high‐risk groups were 77.2%, 64.0%, and 66.6%, respectively. For treatment response, RUNX1‐RUNX1T1 , FLT3‐ITD , and TP53 mutations independently predicted unfavorable to VEN‐HMAs therapy. Multivariable analysis identified NRAS and PTPN11 mutations as independent adverse prognostic factors for overall survival, while achievement of CR/CRi after the first treatment course and receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) were favorable predictors. Based on molecular status, patients were stratified into three prognostic groups. The median OS was 9.5 months in the TP53 ‐mutant (low‐benefit) group and 21 months in the medium‐benefit group ( TP53 wild‐type with FLT3‐ITD or K / NRAS mutations). The high‐benefit group (wild‐type TP53 , no FLT3‐ITD , and wild‐type K / NRAS ) had a significantly superior OS (not reached) compared to the others ( p < 0.001), while OS between the medium‐ and low‐benefit groups was comparable ( p = 0.096). VEN‐HMAs therapy is associated with high response rates in this real‐world cohort, though treatment response varies substantially by molecular profile. A comprehensive understanding of these influencing factors and the development of refined risk stratification systems require further investigation.

papers.abstract: Abstract Adult glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor that has yet to benefit from advances in immunotherapy. Prior studies report contrasting leukocyte immunophenotypes between tumors and an association between myeloid macrophage infiltration and worse patient outcomes. IL-8, a cytokine with both inflammatory and suppressive roles, was recently associated with M2 macrophage phenotypes in GBM. These observations raise key questions: do GBM macrophages suppress or support other immune cells, is IL-8 in GBM a mechanistic driver of GBM macrophage function, and can IL-8 instruct macrophages in situ within tumors? Here, functional experiments with primary human GBM tumor cells from initial surgical resections showed that IL-8 from GBM contributes to and is sufficient to instruct monocyte-derived macrophages that suppress healthy T cells. Notably, IL-8 protein expression was enriched in aggressive tumors contacting the V-SVZ region and was not associated with increased infiltration of cells expressing the IL-8 receptors CXCR1/CXCR2. Suppressor cells instructed by GBM ex vivo phenotypically matched myeloid macrophages observed in vivo, and neutralizing IL-8 during instruction blocked this and restored T cell proliferation. Analysis of IL-8 RNA showed the cytokine is primarily produced by CD45- tumor cells. These results suggest a model where ongoing IL-8 production by GBM cells maintains an immunosuppressive microenvironment by signaling to myeloid macrophages within the tumor. Immunotherapies relying on T cells should now investigate whether IL-8 blockade prevents instruction of macrophages into tumor-protective suppressor cells.

papers.abstract: Abstract Natural killer (NK) cells offer a promising off-the-shelf platform for cancer immunotherapy, yet their clinical efficacy is often limited by tumor-intrinsic resistance. Here, we show that loss of core microRNA (miRNA) machinery components, Argonaute‑2 (AGO2) or Ankyrin Repeat Domain 52 (ANKRD52), renders tumor cells hypersensitive to NK cell-mediated killing in both co-culture and xenograft models. Mechanistically, genetic ablation of Ago2 or Ankrd52 impairs miRNA-mediated silencing of critical mitochondrial apoptotic regulators and NK-cell-associated ligands in tumor cells, exemplified by the disrupted repression of pro-apoptotic Bim transcripts by miR-24 and miR-29b, thereby unleashing rapid TNF-α-driven apoptosis. Additionally, metabolic and ultrastructural analyses demonstrate collapsed membrane potential, diminished ATP levels, and fragmented mitochondria in Ago2- or Ankrd52-mutant tumor cells, accompanied by a lower apoptotic threshold upon TNF-α or NK cell challenge. Genome‑wide CRISPR library screen further revealed a selective fitness dependency on mitochondrial electron‑transport and ATP‑synthase genes in mutant tumor cells. Collectively, these findings define defective miRNA machinery as a tumor‑intrinsic vulnerability that couples mitochondrial fragility with increased NK-mediated cytotoxicity, nominate miRNA‑pathway status as a predictive biomarker, and propose that co‑targeting mitochondrial metabolism or apoptosis may potentiate NK‑cell therapies.

papers.abstract: Early detection of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is hindered by a lack of noninvasive biomarkers for precancerous lesions. Here, we report a circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation approach for early esophageal neoplasia detection. In prospective community screening, the assay achieved standardized sensitivity of 78% at 79% specificity for the clinically actionable endpoint of high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia (HGIN) or ESCC, with stage-specific sensitivities of 76% for HGIN and 86% for ESCC. Genome-wide methylation profiling reveals HGIN as an early epigenetic reprogramming stage. Integrative spatial and single-cell RNA sequencing reveals pronounced remodeling of the endothelial-proximal epithelial cell population, whose methylation signatures are detected in cfDNA. Guided by these findings, we develop an 11-gene cfDNA methylation panel that shows robust discrimination of early-stage ESCC across three retrospective case-control sets and an independent screening-derived case-control set. Together, these results demonstrate that our cfDNA methylation panel has promising utility for early ESCC detection.

papers.abstract: Many tumors remain poorly responsive to immune checkpoint blockade. The metabolic microenvironment in tumors can mediate immunosuppression by failing to sustain productive cytotoxic lymphocyte function. Here, we showed that a coordinated ketogenic-fasting (KF) regimen sensitized immune-refractory tumors to PD-1 blockade by integrating distinct metabolic and microbial effects of ketogenic diet (KD) and intermittent fasting (IF). The KF combination established a distinct immunometabolic state that could not be fully recapitulated by either KD or IF intervention alone. KF induced systemic glucose restriction while preserving intratumoral glutamine availability and selectively upregulating the glutamine transporters SLC38A1 and SLC38A2 in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells and NK cells, fueling interferon-STAT1 signaling and effector activity. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified KF-associated cytotoxic lymphocyte states characterized by enhanced nutrient access signatures, increased effector function, and reduced terminal dysfunction. Microbiota depletion attenuated KF-mediated tumor control without abolishing intratumoral glutamine enrichment. Fecal microbiota transfer and monocolonization identified Odoribacter splanchnicus as sufficient to restore tumor control and cytotoxic T-cell activity in microbiota-depleted hosts. Mechanistically, O. splanchnicus was linked to host polyamine remodeling and indole-3-lactic acid, which supported durable CD8+ T-cell functions distinct from the glutamine-driven effector arm. KF enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy in immune-cold tumor models, and public human datasets showed concordant associations between glutamine context, Odoribacter abundance, and immunotherapy response. Together, these findings identify a diet-responsive host-microbiota metabolic mechanism that stimulates antitumor immunity and sensitizes immune-cold tumors to immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Automated classification of glioblastoma (IDH-wt, WHO CNS Gr.4) histopathologic sub-regions in whole slide images (WSI) is essential for quantitative tumor characterization, but faces substantial challenges from intra-tumoral heterogeneity and inter-observer annotation variability. The AI-RANO & RANO-Pathology working groups organized BraTS-Path 2024, representing the first international benchmarking environment and publicly available spatially annotated dataset, towards promoting the development and fair evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models to classify specific sub-regions: cellular tumor, pseudopalisading necrosis (PN), microvascular proliferation, geographic necrosis, infiltration into the cortex, and white matter penetration (WM). Multi-institutional H&E-stained WSIs had reference standard samples generated by eight expert neuropathologists, following a rigorous peer review protocol, resulting in 309,118 data samples (training/validation/hold-out testing: 96,485/62,387/150,246). Quantitative performance evaluation of six AI approaches was conducted based on multiple metrics, including Accuracy and Matthew's correlation coefficient (MCC). A robust statistically-aware ranking strategy offered statistical significance of the final rankings. Top-performing approaches employed common strategies, including large pre-trained models, ensembling, and extensive data augmentation, reporting Accuracy=0.69 and MCC=0.58. Key challenges included severe class imbalance, hampering minority class performance, and inter-annotator variability, especially for ambiguous sub-regions such as PN or WM. BraTS-Path represents a valuable public resource for glioblastoma histopathologic sub-region assessment. Our findings indicate the specific task remaining an open research problem, highlighting the influence of rare sub-regions, the absence of a consistent "gold standard" annotation protocol, and the potential of foundation models to improve generalization, guiding future research toward developing more reliable AI tools for quantitative neuropathology.

papers.abstract: The present study compared the effects of high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) with automated volume guarantee (HFOV-VG) versus careful manual high-frequency tidal volume (VThf) monitoring (HFOV-VM) on the incidences of hypo/hypercarbia in neonates. In this open-labeled, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 60 neonates failing conventional mechanical ventilation were allocated to receive HFOV-VG (n = 30) versus HFOV-VM (n = 30) as a rescue mode. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia at 1 h. Secondary outcomes were incidences of hypo/hypercarbia at 6/12/24/48 h and beyond, time-specific trends for partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO2), delivered VThf and mean airway pressure (MAP), cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) and regional cerebral oxygenation (CrSO2), duration of respiratory support, and incidences of in-hospital adverse events. Stata 18 was used for an intention-to-treat analysis. The incidence of hypo- or hypercarbia at 1 h of intervention was 15/30 (50%) in the HFOV-VG and 13/30 (43%) in the HFOV-VM groups (p = 0.61). No differences were observed in the incidences of hypo- or hypercarbia anytime during HFOV. Time-specific pCO2, VThf, and MAP were similar. On regression analysis, the only significant predictor for pCO2 at 1 h was the baseline pCO2 level in both the groups. No difference was observed in ACA-CBF, CrSO2, duration of respiratory support, and in-hospital adverse events including mortality. There was no difference in the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia with HFOV-VG versus HFOV-VM at 1 h and throughout the duration of ventilation with a similar rate of complications when used as a rescue therapy. papers.abstract: Background: Cancer treatment intent sets expectations and influences treatment intensity for patients with cancer and oncology clinicians. It is not known what probability-of-cure threshold oncology clinicians use when considering a treatment to have a curative intent. The objective of this study was to determine the lowest probability of cure needed for solid tumor and hematologic oncology clinicians to consider cancer treatment curative in intent. Methods: This study was part of a cross-sectional survey of oncology clinicians (physicians and advanced practice providers [APPs]) at a comprehensive cancer center in the United States. Participants answered the question, “What is the lowest probability of cure for you to consider a cancer treatment to be of curative intent?” by providing a whole-number percentage between 0% and 100%. Results: The overall survey response rate was 66% (245 of 369 eligible clinicians), with 195 (80%) participants completing the curative intent question. Most responders were aged ≤49 years (n=137; 70.3%), female (n=124; 63.6%), and physicians (n=98; 50.3%). Solid tumor oncology clinicians reported a median probability of cure of 35% (IQR, 20%–75%), while hematologic oncology clinicians reported a median probability of 34% (IQR, 20%–70%) ( P =.90). Physicians across both specialties reported a lower probability of cure necessary for treatment to be considered curative in intent than APPs (median, 20% [IQR, 10%–40%] vs 50% [IQR, 30%–80%]; P <.001). Multivariable regression analysis showed that APPs (odds ratio, 2.88; P <.001) and clinicians of Asian race (odds ratio, 1.83; P =.01) were independently associated with a higher probability of cure required for treatment to be considered curative in intent. Conclusions: Our study revealed high variability in how clinicians dichotomize probability of cure into cancer treatment intent, with a significant discrepancy between APPs and physicians. This level of heterogeneity highlights the need to have consistent communication and appropriate expectation setting for patients, caregivers, and other health care professionals.

papers.abstract: The APOBEC3 family of cytidine deaminases, originally evolved for antiviral defense, functions as a potent source of somatic mutations in human malignancies. Although the genomic footprints of APOBEC3 were deciphered over a decade ago with characteristic mutational signatures (single-base substitution [SBS]2 and SBS13), their clinical significance is only now becoming apparent, shifting from a descriptive hallmark of mutagenesis to a potential predictor of therapy outcomes. Emerging evidence from landmark studies reveals that apolipoprotein B mRNA editing enzyme, catalytic polypeptide-like (APOBEC)-associated mutational signatures are associated with acquired resistance to targeted therapies and are an emerging biomarker of response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Mechanistically, therapy-induced activation of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B drives the evolution of drug-tolerant persister cells and generates genomic diversity from which resistant clones emerge-a phenomenon demonstrated across epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitor resistance in lung cancer, endocrine therapy resistance in breast cancer, and androgen receptor blockade resistance in prostate cancer. Concurrently, studies have shown that APOBEC mutational signatures are associated with ICI benefit, including in tumor mutational burden-adjusted analyses, most notably in urothelial carcinoma and non-small-cell lung cancer. In this study, we review this emerging paradigm, focusing on the newly established mechanisms and clinical findings. We further address the translational hurdles of detecting APOBEC mutational signatures in clinical practice and emerging therapeutic strategies, including oligonucleotide-based inhibitors and synthetic lethality. Finally, we discuss standardizing APOBEC mutational signature detection for clinical use, including developing liquid biopsy-based dynamic monitoring, and designing prospective trials with APOBEC mutational signature-based stratification.

papers.abstract: BCR::ABL1 is the oncogenic driver of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph + ) acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), with BCR::ABL1 p210 and p190 being the predominant isoforms. Asciminib, an inhibitor that specifically targets the ABL myristate pocket (STAMP), has demonstrated efficacy in both pre-clinical and clinical studies against p210-driven CML, including cases where resistance mediated by ATP-pocket mutations has developed during prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. The resistant mutation profile of asciminib is currently considered largely distinct from that of ATP-competitive TKIs. In our study, we demonstrate that several ATP-pocket mutations, including the V299L, F311I, T315I, and F317C/L, confer high levels of resistance to asciminib in the p190 isoform (> 1000-fold increase in LD50asciminib values compared to non-mutated BCR::ABL1 p190), but remain sensitive when occurring in the p210 isoform. The T315A was the only tested mutation in BCR::ABL1 p190 sensitive to asciminib. Furthermore, cells expressing BCR::ABL1 p190 mutations exhibited decreased kinase inhibition following STAMP treatment, indicative of an active kinase. Analogous results were obtained for MK-4208 (formerly known as TERN-701), a clinically active investigational STAMP compound. In the BCR::ABL1 p190 setting, this work reveals an overlapping resistance profile between STAMP compounds and TKIs, with important considerations for STAMP-based therapy. It challenges two key assumptions: that asciminib dose escalation can overcome resistant ATP-pocket mutations and that targeted therapy sensitivity profiles are equivalent between the p190 and p210 isoforms.

papers.abstract: Reactivation of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) is a validated therapeutic strategy for sickle cell disease (SCD) and β-thalassemia. Cereblon (CRBN)-dependent molecular-glue degraders of HbF repressors are advancing clinically, but all share an immunomodulatory imide drug (IMiD) backbone and its class liabilities. We show that SH6, a non-IMiD small-molecule degrader, consistently induces HbF in erythroid cell lines, primary healthy-donor, SCD, and β-thalassemia CD34⁺-derived erythroid cells, and humanized NBSGW mice, at nanomolar to low-micromolar concentrations. When all compounds were tested at a matched 0.25µM concentration, HbF induction by SH6 was comparable to that of decitabine and greater than that of hydroxyurea, pomalidomide or thalidomide. HbF induction is CRBN/proteasome-dependent and associated with simultaneous degradation of the γ-globin repressors ZBTB7A and BCL11A. These findings provide proof of concept for IMiD-independent pharmacologic HbF reactivation and support further study of SH6 as a mechanistically distinct tool compound.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Accurate preoperative evaluation of tumor extension in olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB) is critical for optimizing surgical planning, particularly for predicting unexpected intracranial and contralateral invasion. However, discrepancies between preoperative imaging and postoperative pathology remain a challenge. This study compares preoperative imaging with detailed pathological evaluation of anatomically oriented specimens to assess ONB progression, characterize patterns associated with unexpected invasion, and improve surgical strategies. Methods This retrospective study analyzed 58 ONB patients who underwent endoscopic transnasal resection at Jikei University Hospital between January 2018 and March 2024. Preoperative computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging were reviewed by a radiology specialist and compared with postoperative pathological evaluation of anatomically oriented resected specimens. Tumors were classified using Kadish staging and Hyams grading. Results The cohort had a median age of 53 years (range, 29–85 years), with 67.2% male participants. Preoperative staging classified 37.9% of the cases as Kadish C. Among 36 cases preoperatively staged as Kadish A or B, eight (22.2%) exhibited occult intracranial involvement. Unexpected contralateral invasion was observed in five cases, all Kadish C, frequently associated with tumor progression through bony transition areas at the skull base and nasal septum junction. Tumor invasion into the crista galli was identified in six cases, with one case suggesting metastatic spread rather than direct invasion. Conclusions Occult intracranial involvement in Kadish A and B cases may warrant consideration of skull base resection even in early stages. Contralateral invasion was limited to Kadish C and may support consideration of bilateral skull base resection in selected cases where preoperative imaging demonstrates intracranial extension and tumor proximity to key skull base transition areas. Preserving crista galli integrity during resection facilitates detailed pathological evaluation and may contribute to more accurate staging and prognostic assessment.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Gastrointestinal (GI) follicular lymphoma (FL) is a rare disease, accounting for less than 5% of GI non‐Hodgkin's lymphomas (NHL). We conducted a multi‐institutional study to clarify baseline features, common practices, and survival outcomes in primary GI FL. Methods We performed a retrospective analysis of patients with primary GI FL from 8 North American institutions. Progression‐free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and progression of disease at 24 months (POD24) were assessed. Results Two hundred and two patients were included in the analysis. Median follow up was 5.6 years. Median age at diagnosis was 60 years (range: 51–68) with a 1:1 male to female ratio. For those observed, median time to first treatment was 4.5 years. For those treated, overall response rate was 93% ( n = 112) and median time to second‐line treatment was 3.9 years. Patients who were initially observed had similar OS to those who were treated up‐front. Age ≥ 60, histologic Grade 3A, and hemoglobin < 12 g/dL at diagnosis were independent predictors of inferior survival. Based on these results, we created the GI‐FLIPI score, a prognostic index using these three readily available clinical factors to help predict outcomes in patients with GI FL. Median OS was significantly shorter in the high‐risk group compared to intermediate‐ and low‐risk groups, with a c‐index of 0.767. Conclusions This multi‐institutional analysis describes characteristics of a large cohort of patients with GI FL. The GI‐FLIPI score shows promise with high prediction accuracy and may help guide management in the future.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Breast neuroendocrine neoplasms (Br‐NENs) are rare breast tumors with substantial clinicopathological heterogeneity. The prognostic implications of the 2019 World Health Organization (WHO) classification remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of true breast neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) and invasive ductal carcinoma with neuroendocrine differentiation (IDC‐NE) under the 2019 WHO framework. Methods We retrospectively analyzed a pathology‐reviewed single‐center cohort of 123 patients, of whom 121 were included in survival analyses, and a separate population‐based cohort of 498 patients from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Institutional cases were reassessed according to the 2019 WHO criteria, whereas SEER tumor groups were defined using registry‐reported International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, Third Edition (ICD‐O‐3) morphology codes. Survival outcomes were compared using Kaplan–Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness, while exploratory propensity score matching (PSM) analyses compared IDC‐NE with conventional invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC). Results In the single‐center cohort, true NENs showed more aggressive clinicopathological features and were associated with poorer survival than IDC‐NE. In the SEER cohort, 498 patients were included, comprising 323 with registry‐defined NEN and 175 with registry‐defined IDC‐NE. NEN showed more aggressive characteristics, including a higher rate of distant metastasis at diagnosis. After adjustment for age, stage, year of diagnosis, and race, registry‐defined NEN was independently associated with worse overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.62, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.14–2.32) and breast cancer‐specific survival (HR = 2.00, 95% CI 1.30–3.06). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Conclusion Breast NENs were associated with poorer outcomes than IDC‐NE in the pathology‐reviewed cohort. The SEER analysis provided complementary population‐based prognostic evidence for registry‐defined tumor groups. Exploratory PSM analyses did not identify a statistically significant survival difference between IDC‐NE and conventional IDC.

In this paper we review the current evidence for this. We also review data on the effects of embryonic tissue extracts on cancer cells in vitro and in vivo, and discuss potential therapeutic implications.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Venetoclax‐based regimens (VEN) have been widely adopted as frontline therapeutic options for elderly patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, comprehensive real‐world comparisons of VEN with conventional intensive or reduced‐intensity chemotherapy remain limited. Methods In this multicenter retrospective study, we evaluated treatment patterns and outcomes in 1370 patients with newly diagnosed AML. Patients were classified into three cohorts according to their frontline treatment: intensive chemotherapy (IC), reduced‐intensity chemotherapy (rIC), or VEN. Analyses were performed in both the overall cohort and elderly patients (aged ≥ 60 years), including baseline comparisons, uni‐ and multivariable analyses, and subgroup analyses. Results Baseline characteristics differed substantially among treatment cohorts; patients treated with VEN were older and had a higher prevalence of adverse‐risk disease than those receiving IC or rIC . In the overall cohort, VEN achieved an overall response rate ( ORR ) comparable to IC and higher than rIC (74.3% vs. 60.2%, p = 0.034). Among elderly patients, VEN was associated with a higher ORR than rIC (75.7% vs. 50.5%, p = 0.001), and the favorable ORR findings remained significant after correction for multiple testing. VEN was also associated with a lower 60‐day early‐death rate than rIC in elderly patients (1.4% vs. 20.0%, p < 0.001), suggesting better early treatment tolerability. Median event‐free survival was longer with VEN than with rIC in the primary elderly cohort analysis (9.6 vs. 6.6 months, p = 0.031), and this difference persisted in a sensitivity analysis censoring at allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, although it was attenuated in landmark and propensity‐score‐based sensitivity analyses. Overall survival did not differ significantly between the two cohorts (15.9 vs. 11.0 months, p = 0.102). Conclusion The higher response rate and lower early mortality with VEN were the most consistent findings, whereas comparative survival outcomes were considered supportive but exploratory.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognised as a key modulator of cancer development, progression, and treatment response. However, clinical studies remain limited, especially in osteosarcoma (OS), the most common bone cancer in children and adolescents. In this study, we analysed GM diversity, composition, and predicted function in a small OS cohort ( n = 18) using 16S rRNA gene sequencing of stool samples collected at diagnosis, during chemotherapy, and post‐treatment. Microbial profiles were compared to healthy controls. Alpha diversity was assessed via ASVs, Shannon, inverse Simpson, and Faith's index; beta diversity via Bray‐Curtis and UniFrac distances. We examined associations between GM profiles and clinical variables (age, gender, BMI, tumour volume, outcome) and systemic inflammation (e.g., C‐reactive protein, CRP) using PERMANOVA, LEfSe, and Kaplan–Meier analysis. At diagnosis, OS patients showed reduced diversity and a distinct GM signature—depletion of anti‐inflammatory genera ( Blautia, Faecalibacterium, Roseburia ) and enrichment of potentially pro‐tumorigenic taxa ( Collinsella, Streptococcus ), which correlated with elevated CRP. Baseline GM composition stratified patients by long‐term outcome, with specific taxa and predicted pathways linked to event‐free survival. Chemotherapy induced transient dysbiosis, notably affecting Lactobacillus and Enterococcus , with partial recovery post‐treatment. This is the first study to track GM alterations in OS patients across the disease course, extending current knowledge beyond preclinical models. As one of the few longitudinal microbiota studies in oncology, it highlights GM's potential as a biomarker, shedding light on the mechanisms underlying OS pathogenesis, though findings require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The CCL21/CCR7 chemokine axis is implicated in lymphocyte trafficking and cancer metastasis, yet its specific role and molecular mechanism in the pathogenesis of diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remain poorly defined. Methods CCR7 expression was assessed in clinical samples by immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry. In vitro functional assays and molecular techniques were employed in DLBCL cell lines to investigate the CCL21/CCR7 axis. Downstream mechanisms were investigated through RNA sequencing, Co‐immunoprecipitation (Co‐IP), and rescue experiments using the Wnt/β‐catenin inhibitor XAV‐939. Results CCR7 was significantly overexpressed in aggressive DLBCL and correlated with advanced disease stage and poor prognosis. The CCL21/CCR7 axis significantly promoted tumor cell migration, invasion, resistance to apoptosis, and mesenchymal‐like phenotypic changes. Transcriptomic profiling revealed the Wnt/β‐catenin pathway as the most significantly enriched downstream target. Mechanistically, CCL21/CCR7 activation was associated with enhanced Wnt/β‐catenin signaling and a potential physical association between CCR7 and β‐catenin‐containing protein complexes. Inhibition of Wnt/β‐catenin signaling attenuated CCL21‐induced malignant phenotypes. As a potential therapeutic intervention, the anti‐CCR7 monoclonal antibody CAP‐100 attenuated CCR7‐associated signaling, inhibited Wnt/β‐catenin activation, reversed mesenchymal‐like phenotypic changes, and suppressed the malignant behaviors of DLBCL cells in vitro. Conclusion Our study provides novel insights into DLBCL pathogenesis by suggesting that the CCL21/CCR7 axis contributes to tumor aggressiveness at least partly through activation of the Wnt/β‐catenin pathway, leading to mesenchymal‐like phenotypic remodeling. These findings support CCR7 as a potential therapeutic target and suggest that antibody‐mediated CCR7 blockade warrants further in vivo validation.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Head and neck mucosal melanoma (HNMM) is a rare, aggressive malignancy with high recurrence rates and limited prospective data to guide postoperative management. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) have reshaped melanoma treatment, their survival impact in resected HNMM remains poorly defined. We evaluated real‐world outcomes after curative‐intent surgery and the association of adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy with survival. Methods We retrospectively identified patients with HNMM who underwent curative‐intent surgery from 1990 to 2024. Overall survival (OS) and progression‐free survival (PFS) were estimated from surgery using Kaplan–Meier methods. Univariable Cox models evaluated associations of adjuvant ICI with survival. Results Among 89 patients, median follow‐up was 38 months (IQR, 18–60). Most tumors arose in the nasal cavity or paranasal sinuses (72/89, 81%); 23 (26%) had T4 disease and 7 (8%) had regional nodal metastases. Among tested patients, BRAF, NRAS, and KIT alterations were identified in 4/37 (11%), 7/25 (28%), and 0/28 (0%), respectively. Median tumor mutational burden was 3.45 mutations/Mb (IQR, 2.15–7.95; n = 10) and median PD‐L1 tumor proportion score was 0.5% (IQR, 0%–1%; n = 6). Seventeen patients (19%) received adjuvant ICI, including anti–PD‐1 monotherapy ( n = 10), CTLA‐4 monotherapy ( n = 1), or combination anti–PD‐1/CTLA‐4 therapy ( n = 6); 48 (54%) received adjuvant radiotherapy. Two‐ and 5‐year OS were 66% and 46%, respectively; corresponding PFS estimates were 65% and 46%. Adjuvant ICI was not associated with improved OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.69; 95% CI, 0.31–1.55; p = 0.37) or PFS (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.50–2.21; p = 0.88). Initial progression patterns were broadly similar between groups. Conclusions In this single‐institution cohort of surgically treated HNMM, adjuvant ICI was not associated with improved OS or PFS. Patterns of initial disease progression were similar between treatment groups, underscoring the need for more effective peri‐operative strategies.

papers.abstract: Rural-dwelling patients with pancreatic cancer (PC) and a higher Social Deprivation Index (SDI) score may be less likely to receive guideline-concordant care (GCC) than patients living in urban areas. We hypothesized that SDI score and rurality would affect the receipt of GCC among patients with PC. The North Carolina Central Cancer Registry was queried to identify patients with PC from 2004 to 2019. GCC was defined by National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines for PC/Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results staging as localized disease (surgery/chemotherapy), regional disease (at least chemotherapy), or distant disease (chemotherapy and/or palliative care). Multivariable regression assessed the impact of patient-level factors, SDI score, and geographic location on the receipt of GCC. The cohort included 3595 patients with PC: 2532 (70%) urban and 1063 (30%) rural dwellers. Most had regional disease at diagnosis (n = 1871; 52%), were aged 65-79 years (n = 2021; 56%), were female (n = 1891; 53%), were non-Hispanic white (n = 2619; 73%), and had a medium SDI score (n = 1767; 49%), a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 0 (n = 987; 27.5%), and a Frailty Index of 3+ (n = 976; 27%). GCC was received by 151 (32%) patients with localized disease, 1533 (82%) with regional, and 886 (71%) with distant disease. Across all stages, high (odds ratio [OR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-0.92) and medium (OR 0.82; 95% CI 0.67-1.00) SDI scores were associated with a decreased likelihood of receiving GCC. Among localized patients, those with high (OR 0.43; 95% CI 0.21-0.85) and medium (OR 0.47; 95% CI 0.27-0.81) SDI scores had decreased GCC. There was no association between SDI score and GCC among patients with regionalized and distant disease. Across all stages, there was no association between GCC and geographic location. Social deprivation, not rurality, was associated with a decreased receipt of GCC for patients with PC. Multilevel interventions are needed to modify barriers and facilitators of GCC receipt at a state level.

papers.abstract: Whether a multimodal large language model (MLLM) can identify publishable scientific work is untested. This study evaluated whether GPT-4.1 mini could distinguish Society of Surgical Oncology (SSO) posters that reached full-text publication using poster content alone and examined characteristics associated with conversion. This study retrospectively analyzed 597 posters from the 2022-2023 SSO Annual Meetings. Each poster was scored by GPT-4.1 on five research-quality domains during 30 runs at temperature zero. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Multivariable logistic regression tested whether the score added information beyond poster and investigator characteristics. Of 597 posters, 295 (49.4%) reached full-text publication. The composite score showed modest discrimination (AUC, 0.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57-0.66), with no evidence that performance differed across categories (interaction P = 0.90). Each 5-point increase in score was associated with higher adjusted odds of publication (odds ratio [OR], 1.45; 95% CI, 1.21-1.75), and adding the score to poster characteristics improved discrimination (ΔAUC, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.08). Design rigor, data quality, conclusion validity, and publication potential scores were associated with publication, but novelty was not. Multicenter status, first-author training status, and author sex were not significantly associated with publication. Lower adjusted odds for Hispanic first authors did not persist after multiplicity correction (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.15-0.81). The GPT-4.1 mini scores modestly distinguished posters that reached publication and added information beyond poster characteristics. Multimodal large language models merit further study as instruments for examining and strengthening scholarly work rather than as arbiters of publishability.

papers.abstract: Pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC) is a minimally invasive option for peritoneal mesothelioma (PeM) in patients not eligible for cytoreductive surgery (CRS) and hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC). This bicentric study compared the safety, feasibility, and sex-specific outcomes of standard versus high-pressure/high-dose PIPAC (HP/HD-PIPAC). Patients who had non-resectable epithelioid PeM (ePeM) treated with PIPAC at two German centers were retrospectively analyzed. Group 1 received standard PIPAC (cisplatin 7.5 mg/m2 + doxorubicin 1.5 mg/m2, 12 mmHg), and group 2 received HP/HD-PIPAC (cisplatin 20 mg/m2 + doxorubicin 4 mg/m2, 20 mmHg). Procedural outcomes, postoperative complications, interval from diagnosis to first PIPAC, and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. Uni- and multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with OS. The 46 patients in the study (group 1: 25 patients; group 2: 21 patients) underwent 120 of 132 scheduled PIPAC procedures. The median OS from diagnosis was 48 months overall: 48 months in group 1, and 36 months in group 2. The interval from diagnosis to first PIPAC was shorter in group 2 (2 vs. 20 months; p = 0.009). Severe complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥III) occurred in 6.2 % of group 1 versus 2.9 % of group 2. The median OS was 106 months for the females versus 35 months for the males (p = 0.064). Multivariable analysis identified female sex, bidirectional treatment, and a longer interval between diagnosis and first PIPAC as independent factors associated with improved OS. The HP/HD-PIPAC regimen is feasible and safe. Although no significant survival differences were observed between treatment groups, prospective studies are required to define the optimal timing and integration of PIPAC within multimodal treatment strategies. Findings should be interpreted in the context of the retrospective study design.

papers.abstract: Tumor protein 53 (TP53) mutations, long recognized as harbingers of poor prognosis, drive treatment failure in hematologic malignancies by erecting two mutually reinforcing defense systems. Immune evasion is effected through silencing of death-receptor signaling, crippled antigen presentation, and establishment of a T-cell-exclusionary microenvironment, while a parallel metabolic shield fortifies cells against oxidative, proteotoxic, and replicative stress. Here, we propose that immune evasion and metabolic fortification do not operate in complete isolation, but rather as an integrated defense network with emergent crosstalk nodes. We dissect how the spectrum of TP53 mutations dictates the configuration of this barrier, analyze why mono-modal therapies, from chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells and bispecific antibodies to chemotherapy and BCL-2 homology 3 (BH3) mimetics, have shown limited efficacy to date, and outline a roadmap for rationally designed, multi-node therapeutic combinations that may convert these integrated defenses into selective vulnerabilities. This synthesis offers a conceptual framework that may serve as both a mechanistic compass and a translational guide for tackling the high-risk genotypes in leukemia, lymphoma, and myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS).

papers.abstract: Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer1, in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP)2. Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain-domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR-p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a 'super-inhibitory' effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR-p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

papers.abstract: Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers1,2. However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples3, collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

papers.abstract: Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS-STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a heterogeneous and aggressive hematologic malignancy associated with poor survival despite recent therapeutic advances. To identify novel anti-leukemic agents, we performed a high-throughput viability screen of 10,000 small molecules across 56 genetically diverse primary AML samples. Compounds with similar activity profiles were grouped into Compound Correlation Clusters (CCCs), leading to the identification of CCC163, which includes AML874, as a potent and selective hit. Integrated pharmacological and CRISPR-Cas9 approaches identified the Mediator complex as the molecular target of AML874. We demonstrated that AML874 acts as a selective CDK8/CDK19 inhibitor, disrupting Mediator-dependent transcription. FLT3-mutated AML showed increased sensitivity to AML874, suggesting a subtype-specific vulnerability. Notably, CDK8 inhibition synergized with venetoclax in AML cell lines and patient-derived xenograft models, resulting in enhanced anti-leukemic activity in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish CDK8/CDK19 inhibition as a therapeutically relevant strategy in AML.

papers.abstract: DuoBody®-CD40x4-1BB (GEN1042/BNT312) is an investigational bispecific antibody designed to conditionally activate costimulatory receptors CD40 and 4-1BB on immune cells to induce antitumor immunity. Comprehensive in vitro studies demonstrated that dual target engagement by DuoBody-CD40x4-1BB is required to enhance antigen presentation and T-cell priming. As the expected primary sites of action of DuoBody-CD40x4-1BB are the tumor-draining lymph nodes and the tumor microenvironment, we developed a chimeric bispecific surrogate antibody (chi-CD40x4-1BB) containing the VH/VL sequences of DuoBody-CD40x4-1BB in an Fc-inert mouse IgG2a backbone to enable mechanistic studies in vivo. Chi-CD40x4-1BB retained the functional and pharmacokinetic properties of DuoBody-CD40x4-1BB and showed antitumor activity in MC38 and B16F10-OVA syngeneic tumor models in double knock-in mice that express extracellular domains of human CD40 and 4-1BB. In the MC38 tumor model, chi-CD40x4-1BB elicited peripheral immunomodulation, including activation of CD8⁺ and CD4⁺ T cells as well as B cells. Transcriptomic profiling of tumors and lymph nodes revealed induction of gene expression consistent with CD40 and 4-1BB engagement mainly in the secondary lymphoid organs. Combination of chi-CD40x4-1BB with PD-1 blockade resulted in enhanced antitumor activity beyond the single agents. These findings establish chi-CD40x4-1BB as a relevant surrogate to evaluate the activity and mechanism of action of DuoBody-CD40x4-1BB in vivo. Chi-CD40x4-1BB induces CD40 and 4-1BB costimulation, promoting coordinated innate and adaptive immunity, resulting in antitumor activity that can be potentiated in combination with PD-1 blockade. These results may provide context for clinical investigations of DuoBody-CD40x4-1BB, as monotherapy and in combination with PD-1 inhibitors, in solid tumors.

papers.abstract: PORTEC-4a was the first to incorporate molecular-integrated profile-guided adjuvant treatment in early-stage high-intermediate-risk endometrial cancer (EC), demonstrating non-inferiority. Here, adverse events (AE), health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and sexual health are reported. 564 patients were randomised to molecular-based adjuvant treatment (n = 367) or standard vaginal brachytherapy (VBT, n = 197). In the molecular-profile arm, patients underwent observation, VBT or pelvic radiotherapy according to molecular-integrated profile. HRQoL and sexual functioning were assessed with EORTC QLQ-C30 and EN24 modules and compared with age-matched normative data. Median follow-up was 58.1 months; 523 (92.7%) patients were evaluable. Grade 1-2 AEs were less frequent in the molecular-profile arm at treatment completion compared with the standard arm (28.3% vs. 45.2%, p < 0.01), without differences in grade 3-4 AEs (p = 0.46). Throughout follow-up, treatment-related grade 3-4 AEs were rare (1% vs. 2%). HRQoL remained comparable to normative data over time. Sexual interest/activity was similar between arms, but lower than normative values. 75.5% of patients reported ≥1 reason for sexual inactivity; disease-related sexual inactivity decreased from 24.2% to 9.2% at 3 years. Molecular-guided adjuvant treatment for patients with high-intermediate riskEC is associated with low toxicity, preserved HRQoL and slightly reduced sexual activity due to personal factors (no partner, sex not important in their relationship or partner-related medical issues) rather than their own illness.

papers.abstract: Germline pathogenic BRCA1 variants predispose women to breast and ovarian cancer. Despite accumulation of functional evidence, over half of reported single-nucleotide variants in BRCA1 lack a definitive clinical interpretation. Furthermore, the consistency of variant effects across cell types remains largely unexplored. Here we performed saturation genome editing (SGE) of BRCA1 in HAP1 cells to score 4,113 previously unassayed variants. Additionally, we developed an SGE assay in human mammary epithelial cells (HMECs), allowing comparison of effects across cell lines, drug treatments and genetic backgrounds. We identified 538 variants impacting gene function through distinct mechanisms. HAP1 function scores discriminate between known pathogenic and benign variants with near-perfect accuracy. Intriguingly, however, nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants scored neutrally in HMECs. We show that discordantly scored variants are hypomorphic and confer intermediate cancer risk. Overall, this work demonstrates how performing SGE across cell models improves the functional interpretation of rare variants.

papers.abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis1. IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function2,3, with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities4-8. Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1-3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4-7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

papers.abstract: Disconnects between in vitro and in vivo results in experimental biology have long been recognized as potential hurdles to understanding health and disease. A prototypical example of such a disconnect is the NLRP3 inflammasome, which mediates inflammation in diverse settings of disease and protective immunity1,2. Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro requires two signals: (1) priming by pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as bacterial lipopolysaccharides and (2) activation by molecules that disrupt cellular homeostasis1,3. By contrast, the NLRP3 inflammasome in vivo is activated by lipopolysaccharide alone. The mechanisms that underlie the difference between in vitro and in vivo activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome are undefined. Here we report that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness is a determinant of NLRP3 activities and that in vitro systems using physiological ECM stiffness enable one-signal in vivo-like NLRP3 activities to occur in human and mouse phagocytes. Physiological ECM stiffness induced expression of the transcription factor NRF2, which was found to be necessary for one-signal NLRP3 activation. Mechanistically, we identify Panx1 as an NRF2-regulated gene that promotes NLRP3 activity. Macrophages derived from the stiff matrix of the bone-osteoclasts-had reduced NRF2 levels and impaired NLRP3 activity. Moreover, alveolar macrophages from patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity. Finally, NRF2 was required for antitumour immunity induced by cancer vaccines consisting of NLRP3 agonistic adjuvants. These findings indicate that NRF2 may be a transcriptional checkpoint that controls NLRP3 inflammasome activity.

papers.abstract: Most breast cancers respond poorly to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), and hormone receptor-positive (HR +) tumors, which constitute most diagnoses, are particularly refractory. This review synthesizes evidence on tumor-intrinsic determinants of the immune-cold phenotype in breast cancer under an operational framework designated ICE, comprising three functionally defined domains: Invisibility (failure of antigen generation, presentation, and innate sensing), Coercion (active exclusion and post-infiltration suppression of effector cells), and Exhaustion-by-Metabolism (metabolic attrition of infiltrating lymphocytes). ICE is not proposed as a newly discovered taxonomy of immune evasion; its added value lies in integrating breast-cancer subtype resolution, evidence provenance, systems-level interactions, negative clinical evidence, and mechanism-biomarker-intervention matching within a single operational framework. Four features define this framework. The domains are overlapping rather than sequential, and an explicit assignment rule places multifunctional regulators such as MYC, hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, and lactate in a primary domain while cataloguing secondary effects. Tumor-immune interaction is treated as bidirectional, positioning tumor-intrinsic programs as both causes and consequences of immune pressure. Major mechanistic and translational claims are assigned claim-specific evidence tiers. Resistance to immune-mediated killing, including death receptor loss, is classified as cross-dimensional cytoprotection rather than a recognition defect. Applying this discipline exposes an asymmetric evidence base: antigen presentation defects and metabolic suppression rest on substantial preclinical data with limited clinical validation, several widely cited mechanisms derive from non-breast models, and the translational record includes cross-cancer constraints-failure of IDO1 inhibition in a melanoma phase III trial and minimal STING-agonist monotherapy activity in early mixed-solid-tumor studies-together with breast-cancer-specific negative findings from IMpassion131 and the unfavorable benefit-risk profile of abemaciclib plus pembrolizumab. Cross-dimensional systems-level structures, including the hypoxia-adenylosuccinate lyase-fumarate-STING axis and the tumor-macrophage arginine-polyamine relay, are identified as the most instructive examples of domain interaction, and seven falsifiable predictions are advanced, each specifying a measurable biomarker and a decisive experiment.

papers.abstract: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery. We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02). Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.

papers.abstract: Chemoradiotherapy commonly causes radiation-induced lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, as measured by reductions in absolute lymphocyte count (ALC), absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and hemoglobin level (Hb). We aimed to quantify these hematological toxicities and characterize dose-time-response relationships between temporal changes in peripheral blood biomarkers and radiation exposure to the circulating blood during volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) definitive chemoradiotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Blood biomarker measurements were collected from 93 NSCLC patients, treated between 2018 and 2024, at pre-, during-, and post-treatment time points. Radiotherapy prescription doses were 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 55 Gy in 20 fractions, or 50 Gy in 25 fractions with concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy. Organs at risks were delineated by the TotalSegmentator software. The blood dose-volume histogram was estimated through simulations of blood dynamics using the HEDOS software and VMAT dose accumulation was calculated with the BeamSplitter algorithm. Dose-time-response relationships were modelled by linear and exponentially decaying curves, from which rates of change were extracted and goodness of fit quantified using the R2- value. Baseline blood biomarker values (median ± interquartile range) were (1.8±0.9) × 109/L for ALC, (5.6±3.0) × 109/L for ANC, and 132±19 g/L for Hb. Prior to treatment, 0%, 0%, and 30% of patients exhibited lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, respectively. During treatment, these proportions increased to 71%, 19%, and 77%. Dose-response analysis revealed rates of change at low doses of radiation: -69%/Gy (ALC), -83%/Gy (ANC), and -3%/Gy (Hb), with model fits showing R² values between 0.78 and 0.96. Hematological toxicities were frequent in NSCLC patients treated with VMAT chemoradiotherapy. Radiation exposure was associated with changes in circulating lymphocyte counts and hemoglobin, supporting prospective investigation into reducing circulating blood dose during chemoradiation to mitigate hematological toxicity.
