papers.abstract: To evaluate the clinical significance of morular metaplasia (MM) and its temporal patterns in predicting outcomes of fertility-preserving treatment (FST) among young patients with endometrial hyperplasia (EH) and atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH). Retrospective cohort study. 193 patients aged <40 years with EH or AEH who received progestin-based FST (2020-2025) at a single tertiary hospital. MM classified as: MM‑Bef (present only before treatment, n = 9), MM‑Sus (persistent, n = 4), MM‑Aft (emerged after treatment, n = 11), and non‑MM (n = 169). Complete response (CR) rate, time to response (TTR), and factors associated with CR by Cox regression. Overall CR was 62.5% in MM vs. 69.8% in non‑MM (P = 0.485). MM‑Bef achieved 100% CR, MM‑Sus 50%, MM‑Aft 36.4% (MM‑Aft vs. non‑MM, P = 0.009). Median TTR was 5.0 vs. 6.0 months (P = 0.849). Kaplan‑Meier showed no significant difference (log‑rank P = 0.893). In univariable Cox regression, only EH diagnosis was associated with higher CR (HR=1.515, P = 0.031). MM overall or subgroups was not significant (P > 0.10). MM is not an independent predictor of FST outcomes in young EH/AEH patients. However, temporal patterns of MM may represent potential clinically useful signals. Persistent or treatment‑emergent MM showed numerical trends toward lower response rates and longer TTR, suggesting these patients may benefit from enhanced surveillance. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in larger studies.

papers.abstract: Forkhead box O3a (FOXO3a) plays important roles in tumor development; however, its expression pattern, prognostic significance, and biological function in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain unclear. FOXO3a expression was evaluated in PDAC tissues and correlated with clinicopathological characteristics and patient survival. FOXO3a-overexpressing and FOXO3a-silenced PDAC cell models were established to investigate its actions on cell growth, migratory capacity, and invasiveness. The participation of the WNT/β-catenin pathway was examined using immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and rescue experiments. Xenograft models were employed to validate the impact of FOXO3a in regulating in vivo tumor growth. FOXO3a expression was significantly reduced across both PDAC tissue specimens and cell lines compared with controls. Decreased FOXO3a expression was correlated with advanced tumor stage (P = 0.008), perineural invasion (P = 0.019), and distant metastatic status (P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses demonstrated that low FOXO3a expression independently predicted poor overall survival (HR = 2.068, P = 0.004). High β-catenin expression was also identified as an independent risk factor of poor patient outcome (HR = 1.827, P = 0.014). Functionally, FOXO3a overexpression inhibited PDAC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas FOXO3a depletion promoted malignant behaviors. Mechanistically, FOXO3a suppressed the WNT/β-catenin signaling by decreasing the nuclear accumulation of β-catenin, and pathway activation partially reversed FOXO3a-mediated inhibition. In vivo, FOXO3a overexpression significantly inhibited xenograft growth. FOXO3a downregulation exhibits a significant correlation with dverse clinicopathological features and unfavorable outcome in PDAC. FOXO3a exerts tumor-suppressive effects, at least in part, by negatively regulating the WNT/β-catenin pathway and consequently holds promise as a prognostic marker and targeted therapy for PDAC.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains an incurable disease with an extremely poor prognosis. Tumor resection represents a first-line treatment when possible, but most patients suffer tumor recurrence, the primary cause of mortality. One of the functions of connexin43 (Cx43), a gap junction-forming subunit that also has a role in channel-independent signaling, is the inhibition of Src, an oncoprotein involved in tumor progression and recurrence. We previously developed a Cx43 mimetic peptide TAT-Cx43266-283 that recapitulates the inhibition of Src and exerts antitumor effects in patient-derived and mouse in vitro and in vivo models, and here we aimed to explore its effect in GBM recurrence. Analysis of clinical datasets shows a marked increase of Src activity after the standard of care treatments, suggesting that targeting Src activity could prevent GBM recurrence. Importantly, we found that the combination of tumor resection and TAT-Cx43266-283 extended survival in two syngeneic, immunocompetent GBM resection models, which recapitulated key complementary histological features of GBM. TAT-Cx43266-283 in combination with tumor resection increased tumor cell apoptosis and decreased important hallmarks of GBM recurrence by targeting the specific dominant features in each model, such as aberrant vascularization or tumor infiltration. These effects occurred alongside the recruitment of tumor-associated macrophages and microglia (TAMs) to tumor border and their shift towards an antitumor phenotype. Our findings suggest the possible involvement of the immune system in the antitumor effects of TAT-Cx43266-283 and reveal the efficacy and safety of the intracavitary application of TAT-Cx43266-283 after tumor resection, supporting its potential in a clinical setting.

papers.abstract: To determine the cancer-initiating activity of oncoprotein CIP2A, which is overexpressed in a majority of cancers and promotes cell growth by stabilizing MYC, we established an alveolar type 2 cell-specific CIP2A transgenic mouse line. Among 114 transgenic mice aged 12 months or older, 23 (20.2%) developed lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD)-like disease, significantly higher than in the control mice (3/63, 4.8%). Multi-omic studies revealed enrichment of the oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway in tumor tissues from transgenic mice. CIP2A upregulated phosphorylation of FOXO3A (p-FOXO3A S253) by inhibiting phosphatase PP2A-B56α and promoted FOXO3A mitochondrial translocation. CIP2A-FOXO3A reshaped mitochondrial morphology, activated mitochondrial DNA transcription, and enhanced complexes IV/V activities. OXPHOS inhibitor repressed CIP2A-induced cell proliferation and tumor growth. Moreover, tobacco carcinogens upregulated CIP2A and p-FOXO3A S253 and significantly increased cancer incidence in CIP2A-transgenic mice. These data indicate that CIP2A plays a critical role in mitochondrial regulation and represents a promising therapeutic target for LUADs lacking actionable driver mutations.

papers.abstract: Immune-related hepatitis (IRH) and pneumonitis (IRP) occur more frequently in East Asian versus European patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) allelic variations, which differ substantially between ancestries, have been associated with immune-related adverse events (irAEs) risk and ICI efficacy in European cohorts, but large-scale validation in Asian populations is lacking. Clarifying these ancestry-specific biomarkers is critical for advancing precision immunotherapy. We conducted a single-center retrospective study of 3261 East Asian patients with lung cancer treated with ICIs (2018–2023). Of these, 380 patients developed IRH and 248 developed IRP. Each case group was randomly matched 1:3 with controls without that irAE (IRH: 1,140; IRP: 744), resulting in 1793 patients for HLA genotyping. Time-varying Cox models and landmark analyses assessed irAE-overall survival (OS) associations, adjusting for immortal time bias and clinical covariates. Sample weighted Cox-proportional hazard models were conducted to estimate the associations of HLA alleles with the occurrence of irAE and survival. With a median follow-up of 24.9 months (range 0.2–90 months), we identified two independent predictive factors: (1) Mild IRH (grade 1–2) was significantly associated with prolonged OS (p=0.004), with a median onset time of 2.17 months. This association remained consistent across landmark analyses at 3, 6, 9, 12 months and median onset time, supporting its predictive value. (2) HLA-DQB1*06:01 was independently associated with poorer OS (p=0.0004, false discovery rate: 0.03), an effect observed regardless of IRH occurrence. Notably, HLA-DQB1*06:01 frequency in our cohort (8.5%) was substantially higher than reported in European ancestry (0.7%), consistent with known ethnic differences in HLA architecture. In contrast, we found no significant associations between HLA variants and the risk of developing IRH or IRP, suggesting that HLA’s predictive impact operates through mechanisms distinct from irAE susceptibility. This study provides the first large-scale evidence that mild IRH is an early favorable predictive indicator and HLA-DQB1*06:01 identifies a high-risk subgroup, collectively enabling actionable risk stratification in ICI-treated East Asian patients. The observed ethnic differences in HLA allele frequencies and their distinct associations with survival outcomes underscore the critical need for ancestry-informed precision oncology approaches in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are critical mediators of immunosuppression in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet the tumor-intrinsic signals that drive Tregs activation and immune escape remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify key drivers of epithelial-Tregs communication and elucidate their clinical and therapeutic relevance. We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data using CellChat to map epithelial-Treg interactions. Candidate genes were prioritized through survival analyses and subsequently validated across bulk transcriptomic datasets, immunotherapy cohorts, and a prospective institutional ccRCC cohort. Immune infiltration, pathway enrichment, and genomic alterations were systematically characterized. Spatial associations were examined by multiplex immunofluorescence, while functional roles were evaluated using in vitro assays and an in vivo syngeneic mouse model treated with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1). Among epithelia-Tregs signaling candidates, midkine (MDK) emerged as a core ligand with strong prognostic relevance. MDK was markedly upregulated in ccRCC and associated with advanced tumor stage, aggressive histologic features, and unfavorable survival. High MDK expression defined a distinct immunogenomic phenotype characterized by increased Treg infiltration and altered mutation patterns. Elevated MDK expression was associated with poorer outcomes with PD-1 monotherapy and tyrosine kinase inhibitor monotherapy and showed a similar adverse trend with immune checkpoint inhibitor-based anti-angiogenic combination therapy. Spatial analyses confirmed co-localization of MDK-expressing tumor cells with forkhead box P3+ Tregs. Functionally, MDK promoted tumor cell proliferation and migration and was associated with poorer tumor control during PD-1 blockade in vivo. High MDK expression defines a Treg-enriched, immune-evasive ccRCC phenotype associated with aggressive tumor biology and unfavorable outcomes across both immunotherapy and targeted therapy settings. MDK may serve as a biomarker of adverse disease biology and a potential therapeutic target, although its predictive value for treatment selection requires further validation.

papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) stages pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) but does not read out the treatment-guiding tumour biology, requiring biopsy. Whether an imaging-biology relationship discovered in preclinical MRI holds independently in human CT is unknown. One pipeline was applied to two PDAC cohorts: longitudinal 9.4 T multi-parametric MRI (169 sessions; 1002 image series, 471 quantitative maps) with terminal histopathology in male C57BL/6 mice bearing orthotopic KPC-derived tumours treated with gemcitabine, a dendritic-cell vaccine, both, or neither, and abdominal CT with matched proteogenomics from CPTAC-PDA. Radiomics and frozen foundation-model embeddings were modelled under grouped cross-validation against five pre-specified paired endpoints, with no cross-species transfer of features, weights, or labels. Applied independently, the pipeline recovered four matched molecular endpoints in both species (CD8 infiltration, stromal collagen, CD8:CD68 immune balance, cytolytic activity), with areas under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.938-0.960 in mice and 0.780-0.856 in humans. Survival concordance indices were 0.729 and 0.689. After adjustment for age, stage, and grade, the human imaging score remained independently prognostic (hazard ratio 1.87 per SD, 95% CI 1.32 to 2.66; p < 0.001 [Wald test]; combined concordance index 0.726 versus 0.611 for clinical covariates). Findings held in portal-venous-restricted analysis; frozen embeddings outperformed end-to-end fine-tuning in both arms. One pipeline recovered matched PDAC biology in mouse MRI and human CT, supporting preclinical imaging to nominate non-invasive CT biomarker candidates for biopsy-sparing PDAC trial stratification, pending prospective external validation. papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy has shown limited efficacy against solid tumors, with T cell exhaustion representing a major barrier. Both tonic and persistent antigen-dependent CAR signaling markedly drive T cell exhaustion. We therefore hypothesize that minimizing CAR expression (CE) before tumor entry and inducing pulses of CE within tumors would mitigate exhaustion caused by both signaling modes. Here, we present modular artificial- and natural-antigen-gated (MANAGE) CAR-T cells that employ a fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-sensing synNotch receptor to gate CE. Modulating the dosing schedule of FITC-modified tumor-targeting priming adapters enables tumor-restricted and temporally programmable CE in vivo. Compared with constitutive CAR-T and endogenous-antigen-gated synNotch CAR-T cells, temporally tuned MANAGE CAR-T cells exhibit substantially reduced exhaustion and greater preservation of stem-like phenotypes. MANAGE CAR-T cells primed with an albumin-based adapter achieve complete responses without overt toxicity in immunologically "cold" breast cancer and glioblastoma models. This modular strategy is adaptable to various engineered immune cell modalities.

papers.abstract: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a frequent pathological feature of distal cholangiocarcinoma. The spatial molecular programs associated with PNI are unclear. We aimed to characterize tumor-nerve-immune interactions linked to PNI using spatial transcriptomics and independent validation. Spatial transcriptomics was performed using GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler on six cases of surgically resected distal cholangiocarcinoma (non-PNI, n = 3; PNI, n = 3). Regions of interest included non-PNI tumor regions, surface mucosal tumor regions without neural contact (PNI-surface), and tumor regions adjacent to S100-positive nerves (PNI-perineural). Tumor compartments were enriched by CK19-based segmentation. Differential expression and pathway analyses were performed using iDEP/DESeq2 and Reactome/Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment. Validation at the protein level was conducted using immunohistochemistry in an independent cohort (non-PNI, n = 22 and PNI, n = 82) for nerve growth factor (NGF), CD68, and CD163. Three-dimensional nerve architecture was assessed in nine additional cases using tissue clearing. PNI-associated compartments and non-PNI regions had distinct transcriptional profiles. Compared to that in non-PNI, 109 genes were differentially expressed in PNI-surface (34 up- and 75 downregulated) and 179 in PNI-perineural (64 up- and 115 downregulated). Pathway analyses identified enrichment of immune-, microenvironment-, and neurotrophic-related programs, including NGF-associated signatures. Tumor-cell NGF expression was significantly higher in PNI-positive tumors (median H-score: 215 versus 119, p < 0.0001) and increased with depth in PNI cases (p < 0.0001). Deep invasive regions of PNI-positive tumors saw a significant increase in CD68-positive (median 313 versus 210 cells per high-power field, p < 0.001) and CD163-positive (median 64 versus 40 cells per high-power field, p < 0.01) macrophages. CD163/CD68 ratio increased in deep versus surface regions, specifically in PNI-positive tumors (p < 0.0001). PNI-positive distal cholangiocarcinoma exhibited spatially distinct tumor programs and depth-dependent remodeling involving NGF upregulation and M2-like macrophage enrichment, identifying potential therapeutic targets. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.abstract: Abstract Background : Patients with hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-positive (HER2+) advanced breast cancer (ABC) face a high risk of brain metastases (BMs), yet prospective systemic‑treatment evidence for this subgroup is limited. We conducted a multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial evaluating a chemotherapy-sparing regimen of palbociclib, fulvestrant, trastuzumab, and pyrotinib in patients with HR+/HER2+ ABC and measurable BMs. The interim analysis suggested preliminary intracranial activity with manageable toxicity.Methods: Eligible patients had HR+/HER2+ ABC with measurable BMs and no prior local treatment to the target lesion. The regimen was administered until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death. The primary endpoint was confirmed central nervous system objective response rate (CNS-ORR). Secondary endpoints included overall ORR, progression-free survival (PFS), CNS-PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. We present the final analysis for 32 enrolled patients. Results: From Dec 2020 to Feb 2026, 32 patients were enrolled. For 29 response‑evaluable patients, confirmed CNS‑ORR was 58.6% (95%CI 40.7‑74.5) and overall ORR 62.1% (95%CI 44.0‑77.3). With median follow‑up of 32.5 months, median CNS-PFS was 9.6 months (95% CI: 5.3–13.9), and median overall PFS was 12.3 months (95% CI: 6.8–17.7). OS remained immature (5 deaths; 24‑month‑OS rate 80.7%). Post‑hoc analyses suggested numerically better PFS/CNS‑PFS in chemotherapy‑naïve patients, whereas prior trastuzumab did not impair efficacy. Frequent grade ≥3 adverse events comprised diarrhea (37.5%), neutropenia (28.1%) and leukopenia (15.6%), with no treatment‑related deaths. Conclusions: The chemotherapy-sparing quadruple regimen showed promising intracranial activity, systemic disease control, and manageable toxicity in HR+/HER2+ ABC patients with BMs.

papers.abstract: Disparities in breast cancer screening persist in Harris County, even with the presence of a large health care system. This study examined census tract-level associations between social vulnerability characteristics and model-based mammography prevalence estimates and evaluated predictive modeling as an approach to identify geographic areas that may warrant targeted public health outreach. We conducted an ecological analysis linking census tract-level mammography screening estimates from 2024 CDC PLACES with 2022 CDC SVI data across 1108 Harris County census tracts. Five predictive models were evaluated using a 70/30 train-test split, with performance assessed using R², mean absolute error, and mean squared error. Permutation importance evaluated the relative predictive contribution of SVI characteristics. A spatially blocked cross-validation and an earlier-period analysis using 2020 PLACES/2018 SVI data and were conducted as sensitivity analyses. Bayesian Ridge and multiple linear regression showed the strongest predictive performance (R² = 0.839). Leading predictors were poverty, lack of a high school diploma, racial and ethnic minority status, limited English proficiency, and lack of vehicle access. Spatially blocked cross-validation modestly attenuated Bayesian Ridge performance (mean R² = 0.761 ± 0.090), while the five leading predictors retained the same rank order. Predictor importance differed substantially in the earlier-period analysis. Census tract-level social vulnerability characteristics were strongly associated with PLACES-estimated mammography prevalence. Some leading predictors overlap with sociodemographic information incorporated into the PLACES estimation framework and therefore require cautious interpretation. This predictive modeling study may offer a useful framework to identify areas warranting further assessment and inform targeted outreach and resource allocation. Findings represent ecological associations with model-based estimates rather than individual-level or causal relationships, and external validation is needed to assess broader applicability.

papers.abstract: Mocertatug rezetecan (Mo-Rez; GSK5733584) is a B7-H4-targeting antibody-drug conjugate comprising a humanized anti-B7-H4 monoclonal antibody linked to the topoisomerase I inhibitor rezetecan. In the Phase 1 BEHOLD-1 study (NCT06431594), Mo-Rez demonstrated encouraging antitumor activity in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (objective response rate [ORR], 62%) and recurrent/advanced endometrial cancer (ORR, 67%), supporting further clinical evaluation in Phase 3 studies. The global BEHOLD Phase 3 clinical program consists of five randomized studies evaluating Mo-Rez across ovarian and endometrial cancer treatment settings, with approximately 3,070 patients planned for enrollment. The ovarian cancer studies evaluate platinum-resistant disease (BEHOLD-Ovarian01, NCT07286266), platinum-sensitive disease (BEHOLD-Ovarian02, NCT076684612), and first-line maintenance for non-homologous recombination deficient disease (BEHOLD-Ovarian03, NCT07694427). The endometrial cancer studies evaluate previously treated advanced/recurrent disease (BEHOLD-Endometrial01, NCT07286331) and first-line maintenance for mismatch repair proficient disease (BEHOLD-Endometrial02, NCT07684599). Primary endpoints include progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS), depending on study design. Secondary and exploratory endpoints include safety, pharmacokinetics, biomarkers, immunogenicity, and quality-of-life assessments. Collectively, the BEHOLD program evaluates three therapeutic strategies: replacement of conventional chemotherapy with a B7-H4-directed ADC, combination approaches with bevacizumab or immune checkpoint inhibitors, and use of Mo-Rez as maintenance therapy. Tumor tissue collection across studies enables prospective evaluation of B7-H4 expression and other biomarkers as predictors of clinical benefit. The BEHOLD program represents a comprehensive Phase 3 clinical development effort designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Mo-Rez across multiple ovarian and endometrial cancer settings and to further characterize the clinical relevance of B7-H4 as a therapeutic target in gynecologic malignancies.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer prevention has been demonstrated using aromatase inhibitors (AIs) including exemestane, but menopause-related adverse events can limit adherence. We hypothesized that estrogens are potential biomarkers that could be measured at baseline to predict the probability of AI-related adverse events. Estrone (E1) and estradiol (E2) levels were measured from Mammary Prevention 3 trial baseline serum samples (n = 4111) using liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry. Hot flashes, fatigue, and joint pain were assessed using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v4.0. Severe toxicity (grade ≥3) and moderate toxicity (grade ≥2) were contrasted with less severe toxicity. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) for each symptom (years 1 and 5) and baseline E1 and E2 levels. Women on exemestane with the highest levels of E1 or E2 at baseline were significantly more likely to develop severe hot flashes (E1: ORyr-1 = 3.8, 95% CI 1.6-10.5) and (E2: ORyr-1 = 4.2, 95% CI 1.6-13.1) compared with women in the lowest quartile, with a clear dose-response observed at year 1. Severe joint pain was associated with higher baseline E1 and E2 levels in women on exemestane at year 1 but was only statistically significant for E1 (quartiles 2 and 3). There were no significant associations in the placebo group. Women in the highest quartile of E1 or E2 were significantly more likely to discontinue protocol therapy within the first 12 months, independent of assigned treatment, compared with women in the lowest quartile. Postmenopausal women with elevated estrogen levels who initiate exemestane are at greater risk for the development of severe hot flashes and joint pain and may benefit from measures to limit early discontinuation.

papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose: NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with radiation resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated the dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) inhibitors pyrimethamine and its potent analog, WCDD115, as radiosensitizing agents through disruption of one-carbon metabolism. Patients and Methods: Preclinical studies used NRF2-competent and deficient HNSCC models, clonogenic assays, transcriptomics, metabolomics, pharmacokinetics/toxicity testing, and syngeneic tumor grafts to assess WCDD115 as a novel radiosensitizing agent. In parallel, we conducted an open-label, single-center, window-of-opportunity early phase I clinical trial (NCT05678348) of previously untreated patients with HPV(-) stage III/IV HNSCC to receive pyrimethamine 50mg prior to surgery. Correlative analysis included mass spectrometry, western blotting, and pathway analysis. Results: WCDD115 enhanced radiation-induced DNA damage and suppressed one-carbon metabolism and nucleotide biosynthesis. Parallel mouse tumor studies demonstrated that WCDD115 enhanced the efficacy of radiation in NRF2-competent but not NRF2-deficient tumors. In a clinical trial of neoadjuvant pyrimethamine, DHFR protein expression was enriched post-treatment by a mean fold change of 9.91 (95% confidence interval 8.1 to 12.2), consistent with a strong on-target effect. The drug was well tolerated with no drug-related grade 3-5 adverse events or surgical delays. Conclusions: NRF2 hyperactivity is associated with enhanced one-carbon metabolism which can be therapeutically targeted with DHFR inhibitors to promote radiation sensitization. In HNSCC patients, pyrimethamine achieves potent DHFR inhibition and a favorable safety profile supporting a future phase 2 trial integrating pyrimethamine with definitive radiation-based therapy for NRF2-active HNSCCs.

papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose: Molecular diagnostics are standard of care for most adults with solid malignancies, but implementation in pediatric solid tumors remains inconsistent. The SPROUT (Somatic Profiling for Pediatric Cancer Refining our Understanding and Treatment) Molecular Guidelines Working Group was convened to develop molecular testing guidelines for pediatric solid tumors. Experimental Design: A structured literature review was performed using Covidence to identify relevant clinical studies evaluating molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. The literature and collective clinical experience of the multidisciplinary working group were used to develop consensus recommendations for molecular profiling at diagnosis and at relapse or recurrence. Results: Of 361 manuscripts screened, 41 studies were included for data extraction. Based on the available evidence and expert consensus, recommendations were developed for the use and timing of DNA and RNA next-generation sequencing and methylation profiling across pediatric solid tumors. Conclusions: The SPROUT Molecular Guidelines provide a framework for standardized implementation of molecular diagnostics in pediatric solid tumors. Broad adoption of these recommendations may improve diagnostic precision, reduce variability in molecular testing, and increase opportunities for biomarker-directed therapy and clinical trial enrollment for children with cancer.

papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose: The aim of the study is to clinically evaluate the safety, pharmacodynamic (PD) biomarkers, and efficacy of BI-1808, a first-in-class ligand-blocking, Fcγ receptor (FcγR)–engaging anti-TNFR2 antibody, as a novel immunotherapy approach to enhance antitumor immunity in patients with solid cancer. Patients and Methods: Preclinical modeling in syngeneic tumor models was used to assess the relationship between dose, pharmacokinetics (PK), receptor occupancy (RO), and efficacy, as well as PD biomarkers measured in peripheral blood and tumors. These findings informed dosing and analyses in a first-in-human phase I dose-escalation trial in patients with solid cancers. Results: BI-1808 was safe and well tolerated, showed expected PK, and achieved full RO throughout the 3-week dosing interval. Tumor regression was observed in two patients, one with non–small cell lung cancer and one with gastrointestinal sarcoma. Stable disease was observed in 6 of 21 evaluable patients. Tumor regression was preceded by increases in circulating CX3CR1+CD8+ T cells and tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells, consistent with the activation of antitumor immunity. PD analyses were consistent with the preclinically characterized mechanism of action, including dose-dependent reduction of regulatory T cells, monocyte activation, and serum cytokines indicating myeloid reprogramming, tertiary lymphoid structure formation, and CD8+ T-cell activation. Conclusions: These early clinical findings support further development of ligand-blocking, FcγR-engaging anti-TNFR2 antibodies as a safe and mechanistically distinct cancer immunotherapy strategy. The excellent safety profile of BI-1808 makes it well-suited for combination with other immunotherapies, targeted agents, chemotherapeutics, cell therapies, and antibody–drug conjugates.

papers.abstract: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is a rare, aggressive pediatric malignancy driven by FET::ETS family fusions (EWSR1::FLI1 in >85% of cases) with no established environmental risk factors. We analyzed 2,014 EwS cases and 10,525 cancer-free controls in a two-stage analysis that combined an international genome-wide association study and a case-parent trio study. The combined meta-analysis identified 18 variants at 14 susceptibility loci (9 novel and 5 replicated) with moderate effect sizes (odds ratios ≥ 1.25). Integrative analyses of the EwS loci revealed enrichment of enhancer-like GGAA microsatellites, with evidence for binding of the EWSR1::FLI1 fusion at most loci. EWSR1::ETS knockdown in EwS cell lines resulted in dysregulated genes at susceptibility loci related to skeletal/muscle development, RNA binding/processing, and chromatin regulation. Our findings provide insights into the inherited component of EwS, highlighting a genetic architecture in which common germline variation with moderate effects interacts with somatic EWSR1::FLI1 fusions to promote sarcomagenesis by dysregulating local genes.

papers.abstract: The optimal integration of immunotherapy with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in neoadjuvant treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We integrate paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell RNA sequencing and TCR sequencing data from patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT), chemoradiotherapy (NCRT), or immuno-chemoradiotherapy (NICRT) to investigate how these regimens shape intratumoral CD8+ T cell responses. Favorable responses to NICT are associated with maintenance of pre-existing CXCL13+PD-1+ CD8+ T cells and post-treatment enrichment of a progenitor-like CD8Tex_CXCR4 subset. In contrast, CRT responders show reduced CXCL13+ CD8+ T cells and enrichment of clonally expanded, cytotoxic PD-1- CD8Teff_NIBAN1 cells. These divergent programs are validated in public datasets and independent prospective cohorts. In murine models, radiotherapy limits PD-1+ T cell expansion, whereas induction anti-PD-1 treatment followed by radiotherapy improves tumor control. Together, these findings reveal distinct CD8+ T cell programs associated with response to different neoadjuvant modalities and provide a cellular rationale for optimizing immunotherapy-radiotherapy sequencing.

papers.abstract: Comprehensive profiling of peripheral immune cells has shown prognostic and disease-monitoring value across multiple cancers, but its clinical relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly unresectable HCC, remains insufficiently defined. To address this gap, we performed integrated peripheral immunoprofiling combining T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing, flow cytometry-based T-cell phenotyping, bulk RNA sequencing, and public single-cell RNA-seq analysis in healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients. This design enabled characterization of HCC-associated and stage-associated peripheral immune alterations and identification of immunotherapy-relevant features in unresectable HCC. Single-cell analysis and flow cytometry revealed remodeling of circulating T-cell states in unresectable HCC, including reduced naïve-like compartments, enrichment of Treg-like cells, and increased memory/effector differentiation. TCR repertoire analysis showed reduced diversity, increased clonal dominance, altered V-J gene usage, decreased interindividual sharing, and convergent motif-level alterations, with early CD4+ TCR perturbations in resectable HCC and more pronounced CD8+ repertoire restriction in unresectable disease. Exploratory GLIPH-based motif analysis, HLA inference, and peptide-HLA binding prediction suggested candidate motif-HLA antigen associations involving hepatitis virus-derived antigens and recurrent HCC mutation-derived candidate neoantigens, although experimental validation is required. Bulk RNA-seq of peripheral CD8+ T cells revealed higher Activation/Effector function, Exhaustion, and Anergy signature scores in both resectable and unresectable HCC than in HDs, with no significant differences between the two HCC groups, whereas the Chemokine/Chemokine receptor signature was specifically increased in unresectable HCC. The overall IFN-response signature did not differ significantly among the three groups. Integrative machine-learning models were then developed using 818 peripheral immune-related features. Among them, the random forest (RF) model effectively distinguished healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients, with consistently high sensitivity and area under the curve (AUC) in both cross-validation and an independent validation cohort. In unresectable HCC patients receiving immunotherapy, four features derived from TCR-seq and T-cell subset profiling discriminated responders (CR/PR) from non-responders (SD/PD) in univariate analyses, while multivariate prioritization further highlighted ULBP1 as a consistently prioritized response-associated feature that requires validation in an independent cohort. Overall, this study supports comprehensive peripheral immune profiling as an exploratory framework for identifying stage-associated immune alterations and candidate biomarkers to inform personalized immunotherapy strategies in HCC.

papers.abstract: CA209-8M4 is a prospective phase II trial evaluating the addition of nivolumab to total neoadjuvant treatment (TNT) in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). Patients with LARC (T3-4Nany or TanyN1) up to 12 cm from the anal verge received standard chemoradiation (CRT) followed by chemoimmunotherapy (CIMT): six cycles of standard mFOLFOX6 and nivolumab at 240 mg. We defined a novel primary endpoint, combining pathological complete response (pCR) rate among operated patients and long-term (≥12 months) clinical complete response (cCR) rate for those electing watchful waiting, into a composite endpoint of modified pCR (mpCR) rate. Between April 2019 and March 2024, 29 patients were enrolled, median age 53 years, 72.4% male; 96.6% of tumors were cT3 or cT4, 69.0% cN+, and 96.6% microsatellite stable. Median distance from the anal verge was 7 cm; 51.7% of patients had grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) during CIMT, including one fatality (mesenteric inflammation), attributed most likely to CRT's unresolved toxicity. Immune-mediated AEs occurred in four patients (13.8%): grade 3 diabetes mellitus (1) and grade 1 hepatitis (3), including one with asymptomatic hyper/hypothyroidism. Twenty-eight patients (96.6%) are assessable for mpCR: 6 of the 15 operated achieved pCR, and 13 were not operated with cCR ≥12 months, leading to a 67.9% mpCR rate. With a median follow-up of 43.5 months (range 25.0-84.1+), all 28 assessable pts are alive with no evidence of disease. The estimated 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival rates of the entire group are 93% [95% confidence interval (CI) 84-100] and 97% (95% CI 90-100), respectively. The addition of nivolumab to standard TNT in LARC seems safe and may enhance its effectiveness, with encouraging mpCR and survival rates. A multicenter randomized trial, further evaluating this strategy, is ongoing.

papers.abstract: ARDS comprises distinct inflammatory subphenotypes, including hyper- and hypo-inflammatory forms. Whether these differ in ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) mismatch and response to ventilatory strategies remains unclear. Dual-energy CT enables regional assessment of aeration and perfusion. This experimental study aimed to compare V/Q mismatch between hyper- and hypo-inflammatory subphenotypes, and respective responses to PEEP and prone positioning. In 10 pigs, hypo-inflammatory ARDS was induced by lung lavage followed by injurious ventilation. Hyper-inflammatory ARDS was produced by i.v. endotoxin infusion and fluid loading. Pigs were randomised to hypo- or hyperinflammatory ARDS, with similar oxygenation impairment. Dual-energy CT scans were obtained at individualised low, optimal, and high PEEP settings, in supine and prone positions. V/Q was derived from regional gas and blood volume and classified as low ( 2). Linear mixed-effects models included injury group, PEEP, and posture as fixed effects, and subject as a random effect. Hyper-inflammatory injury showed more severe V/Q mismatch than hypo-inflammatory injury (normal V/Q: 35% [sd=10] vs 51% [8] at low PEEP, supine position; P<0.01). Both PEEP optimisation and prone positioning improved V/Q. Prone positioning reduced high V/Q and dead space in hypo-inflammatory injury (group×posture interaction: F1,50=4.32, P=0.04), whereas PEEP reduced low V/Q and shunt in the supine position independent of ARDS subphenotype. In porcine models of hyper- and hypo-inflammatory ARDS, hyper-inflammatory injury was associated with more severe V/Q mismatch despite similar oxygenation. Distinct responses to PEEP and prone positioning support a subphenotype-tailored approach to ventilatory management.

papers.abstract: The optimal timing of postoperative Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) following brain metastasis resection remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between surgery-to-GKRS timing and overall survival (OS) and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS). We retrospectively analyzed 182 patients who underwent initial postoperative cavity-directed GKRS following brain metastasis resection between May 2007 through February 2025. Surgery-to-GKRS timing was evaluated continuously and using outcome-oriented cutpoint analysis across intervals of 7-60 days. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression, with additional sensitivity analyses evaluating cutpoint stability and potential confounding. The median surgery-to-GKRS interval was 19.5 days. Treatment within 14 days demonstrated the greatest observed OS separation, with median survival of 37.8 versus 15.3 months for patients treated later (log-rank p = 0.0123). This association persisted after multivariable adjustment (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.38-1.00; p = 0.0491) and additional adjustment for calendar year of surgery (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37-0.97; p = 0.037). However, the 14-day threshold did not retain statistical significance after adjustment for outcome-oriented cutpoint selection (p = 0.181). GKRS timing was not significantly associated with LRFS. GKRS within 14 days of brain metastasis resection was associated with substantially longer overall survival, highlighting the potential clinical importance of timely postoperative radiosurgical care. Although the optimal treatment interval remains uncertain, these findings support early referral, efficient multidisciplinary coordination, and minimizing avoidable treatment delays.

papers.abstract: The concept of non-operability in diffuse glioma remains poorly standardized and may reflect institutional experience rather than absolute surgical limitations. We evaluated whether patients previously deemed "non-operable" by outside institutions could undergo awake craniotomy and achieve outcomes comparable to those of patients initially considered operable. We retrospectively analyzed 448 adults who underwent awake function-based craniotomy for a diffuse glioma (2011-2024). Sixty-six patients (14.7%) had previously been considered "non-operable" and were compared with patients initially considered operable. Feasibility, safety, and were assessed using propensity score matching and voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping. Patients in the "non operable group" more frequently had prior oncological treatments, focal neurological deficits, larger tumor volumes, greater midline mass effect, and IDH-wildtype glioblastoma. Despite greater preoperative complexity, feasibility, safety, and efficacy outcomes did not significantly differ between groups, including intraoperative adverse events, surgery-related complications, 6-month postoperative Karnofsky Performance Status score and seizure control, extent of resection, and residual tumor volume. No awake procedure was aborted in the "non-operable" group. Propensity score-matched confirmed these findings. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identified no independent anatomical predictor of prior non-operability designation. In selected patients referred for a second opinion, a prior "non-operable" designation did not preclude safe awake resection, suggesting that non-operability may partly reflect a center-related judgment. Patients initially deemed "non-operable" can achieve outcomes comparable to those of conventionally considered operable patients when managed in specialized high-volume centers with expertise in awake function-based craniotomy. These findings support systematic consideration of referral for a second opinion in such patients.

papers.abstract: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutations are truncal driver events in low-grade gliomas. While multifocal gliomas are presumed to spread metastatically and share identical pathology, the biological nature of IDH mutant multicentric gliomas remains poorly understood. We retrospectively identified patients with radiographically distinct multicentric gliomas where ≥ 1 lesion was IDH-mutant. We analyzed the subset with multi​focal tissue sampling using available histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and next-generation sequencing across distinct foci to render updated CNS WHO diagnoses based on integrated molecular data. Of 46 multicentric IDH-mutant gliomas, eight patients (17%) underwent multifocal sampling. Of six synchronous cases, three exhibited mismatched foundational drivers, one showed divergent clonal evolution (discordant 1p/19q codeletion), and two demonstrated asynchronous malignant progression. Differing pathology between the lesions directly influenced clinical decision-making in three of the synchronous cases. The remaining two cases presented metachronously. Structured review of surgical decision-making in 35 evaluable patients without multifocal sampling revealed that in 71% (25/35) of reviewed cases, tissue sampling of the additional lesion was not pursued for lesion-level (poor stereotactic target, diagnostic uncertainty) or patient-level reasons. In the remaining 29% (10/35), the additional lesion was determined to be amenable to biopsy or resection, yet sampling was deferred on the presumption of pathological concordance with the index lesion. Multicentric IDH-mutant gliomas exhibit significant spatial and temporal heterogeneity driven by diverse oncogenic and clonal evolution. Because radiographic congruence does not guarantee histo-molecular congruence, multi​focal tissue acquisition with detailed morphologic and genetic profiling should become the standard clinical approach whenever feasible to prevent diagnostic misclassification and optimize individualized therapy.

papers.abstract: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C76-linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from Amphidinium sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

papers.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body-irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8+ T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

papers.abstract: Brain metastases affect many patients with solid tumor malignancies. Treatments include surgery, radiation, immunotherapy, and CNS-penetrating chemotherapy. Nonetheless, rates of CNS-related tumor death remain high. Local recurrence after radiosurgery and lesions with a V12 too high for radiosurgery present a particular challenge. The VIGILANT (Vigilant Observation of GLIADEL Wafer Implant) registry prospectively examined use and efficacy of carmustine-releasing wafers which includes patients with brain metastases [1]. Here we present a retrospective analysis of patients with brain metastasis from the VIGILANT registry. Forty-seven patients were observed after surgical resection of brain metastasis and GLIADEL implantation at Wake Forest Baptist Medical Center. Thirty-eight patients underwent treatment for local recurrence following radiosurgery. Nine had lesions treated that were deemed too large for successful primary radiosurgery. Patients were evaluated primarily for overall survival (OS) and progression free survival (PFS) from the date of surgery, and secondarily for adverse events and local progression. Median OS was 23 months. Of 25 deaths, 7 (28%) met criteria for CNS-tumor related etiology. 24 (51.1%) patients had progression during follow up, 6 (12.8%) had local progression. 2 (4.3%) overall had local progression that required additional neurosurgical treatment. Of 9 patients not previously treated with radiosurgery, 4 (44.4%) had no progression. Of 5 patients who received GLIADEL as their upfront cranial intervention, none had local recurrence. 43 patients had adverse events; 2 considered possibly GLIADEL related. In this single-institution retrospective analysis of prospectively collected registry data, patients undergoing resection and carmustine wafer implantation after prior radiosurgery or for lesions considered unsuitable for primary radiosurgery had favorable observed survival (OS 23 months), intracranial progression (1-year local progression rate of 12%), and minimal related adverse-event outcomes.

papers.abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is a lethal, treatment-resistant brain cancer characterized by diffuse brain invasion, complex neuron–glioma signaling, and cellular, molecular, and spatial heterogeneity. Surgery is the current mainstay of treatment, aimed at maximizing tumor cytoreduction, decompressing the brain to improve neurologic function and providing material for analyses to inform prognostication and adjuvant treatment selection. To accurately model GBM surgical resection and tissue sampling in preclinical animal models, we developed the Maximal Safe Intracranial Surgery (MSIS) platform. MSIS integrated a miniaturized neurosurgical resection device and enabled a safe, tunable, and reproducible approach for intracranial tumor resection, multiregional biopsy, and longitudinal tissue sampling in murine models, with stereotactic, sterile, and high-viability tissue collection. MSIS was applied across five distinct orthotopic brain tumor models to reproducibly generate histologically and radiologically representative models of postsurgical GBM. Similar to humans, increasing the extent of resection correlated with improved animal survival, and recurrent growth patterns varied significantly by model type. Transcriptional profiles of matched primary versus postsurgical recurrent tumors revealed enrichment of margin-associated transcriptional states consistent with neuron–glioma signaling. Overall, the MSIS approach offers opportunities to model the standard of care, dissect the spatial and temporal dynamics of GBM, and pair therapeutic discovery with contextual tumor pathobiology. Significance: A clinically derived stereotactic resection platform models surgical resection in glioblastoma, enabling longitudinal tissue sampling and revealing conserved early-recurrence neuron-glioma programs in patient-derived models.

papers.abstract: Canada faces mounting anesthesia workforce pressures, particularly in rural and smaller urban centres. Understanding residents' motivations regarding practice setting, research, and fellowship training is essential for workforce planning. We aimed to update a 2015 national survey to characterize current preferences and temporal shifts among Canadian anesthesiology residents. We conducted an anonymous, cross-sectional survey of residents in accredited Canadian anesthesiology programs (November-December 2024) using Research Electronic Data Capture. Items addressed demographics, practice setting, research experience and intentions, and fellowship plans. Selected responses were compared with 2015 survey items using Chi square tests and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals; all tests used an alpha of 0.05. Ninety-four residents responded (12% response rate). Most preferred academic practice (63%), and half preferred to remain at their training institution (49%). Interest in rural practice was reported by 49%. Although research participation was common during medical school (94%) and residency (83%), only 18% intended to pursue research after residency. Approximately 63% intended to pursue fellowship training. Compared with the 2015 survey, there were significant increases in intention to remain at the same institution (from 35% to 50%; P = 0.02) and residency research participation (from 69% to 83%; P < 0.01), whereas intention to pursue research after residency declined (from 34% to 18%; P < 0.01). Canadian anesthesiology residents continue to favour academic practice and fellowship training, yet fewer plan to integrate research into future careers. These findings highlight opportunities for targeted mentorship, greater research autonomy, financial support, and expanded rural training pathways to align resident priorities with workforce needs.

papers.abstract: The solicitation of same-day consent for participation in clinical research is commonly prohibited by research ethics boards because of concerns about limited decision-making time and patient vulnerability. However, these concerns lack empirical support and restrict both research efforts and patient participation opportunities, particularly in medical specialties such as emergency medicine, critical care, and anesthesiology, in which clinicians and patients interact for the first time on the day of a procedure. We aimed to assess the voluntariness of research consent solicited on the day of surgery compared with consent obtained in advance. We performed a prospective, noninferiority randomized controlled trial examining the voluntariness of informed consent to participate in a low-risk clinical research trial at Women's College Hospital in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The trial design included active deception (invitation to participate in a fabricated research trial) to capture authentic measurements of participants' perceptions of any perceived coercion. We randomized 114 patients scheduled to undergo anterior cruciate ligament repair for recruitment into a fabricated low-risk perioperative research trial at one of two time points: at a virtual preanesthesia clinic appointment in advance of the day of surgery, or on the day of surgery. Regardless of their decision, all participants received the (same) standard of care. Overall, 71/114 patients (62%) either consented to participate in the fabricated trial or declined participation but consented to a feedback session during which perceptions of coercion were assessed. Greater participation was observed among patients approached on the day of surgery (fabricated trial, 26/58 [45%]; feedback session only, 18/58 [31%]) than in advance (fabricated trial, 17/56 [30%]; feedback session only, 10/56 [18%]). Perceived coercion, measured using two validated psychometric instruments, did not differ between patients recruited on the day of surgery and those recruited in advance. A subset of patients in each group reported modest perceptions of undue influence, but regardless of recruitment time point, these patients demonstrated their agency to decline participation. Our findings suggest that restrictive same-day consent policies, when based on concerns regarding undue influence, may represent a structural barrier to participation in low-risk trials that lacks empirical justification. 1) Open Science Framework ( 46twc ); first submitted 17 March 2023; 2) ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT07380035 ); first submitted 16 January 2026.

papers.abstract: Post-ICU care often misses patients unable to attend in-person clinic visits. Remote assessments of physical function might increase access to ICU aftercare. We investigated whether patient-reported disability predicts handgrip strength (HGS) and the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) distance with sufficient clinical accuracy. This secondary analysis of the stepped-wedge cluster-randomised Enhanced Recovery after Intensive Care trial included patients from 10 German ICU clusters who completed the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 plus either HGS, the 2MWT, or both, 6 months after ICU discharge. Relationships between WHODAS 2.0, HGS, and 2MWT were analysed using scatter plots, correlation coefficients, linear regressions, and Bland-Altman plots. Predictions of HGS and the 2MWT were compared with the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for both measures. Of 1463 enrolled patients, 620 were analysed. The median WHODAS 2.0 sum score was 11 (Q1, Q3: 3, 22). The median HGS, expressed as a percentage of the expected value (%exp), was 70.6%exp (Q1, Q3: 54.4, 85.6), and the median 2MWT distance was 73.7%exp (Q1, Q3: 61.5, 85.8). The 2MWT was not completed by 59% of patients. Higher disability was moderately correlated with lower HGS (Spearman %exp: -0.41) and shorter 2MWT distance (Spearman %exp: -0.47). In multivariable regression models, the WHODAS 2.0 sum score predicted HGS in kg (β: -0.27 [95% CI: -0.33 to -0.22]; P<0.001) and 2MWT distance in m (β: -1.94 [95% CI: -2.37 to -1.51]; P<0.001), but the limits of agreement exceeded the MCIDs. With increasing disability, HGS and 2MWT performance declined, although correlations were moderate and uncertainty of predictions exceeded MCIDs of both instruments. Remote WHODAS 2.0 assessments cannot replace in-person physical function testing. NCT03671447.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Interstage infants with single‐ventricle (SV) physiology following Stage I palliation represent a high‐risk population for noncardiac procedures requiring anesthesia. Data comparing perioperative outcomes by shunt type remain limited. Aims Describe anesthetic management, perioperative complications, and postoperative outcomes in interstage SV infants undergoing noncardiac interventions and compare outcomes between right ventricle‐to‐pulmonary artery (Sano) and modified Blalock‐Taussig‐Thomas shunt (mBTTS) patients. Methods We performed a retrospective single‐center cohort study of interstage SV infants with Stage I palliation undergoing noncardiac surgery or nonsurgical procedures requiring anesthesia between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were stratified by shunt type. Results A total of 208 noncardiac interventions in 120 interstage SV infants were analyzed; 136 (65.4%) encounters in 86 Sano patients and 72 (34.6%) encounters in 34 mBTTS patients. Compared with mBTTS infants, Sano patients underwent interventions at a younger age (57 [IQR 40–83] vs. 105 [59–278] days, p < 0.001) and lower weight (3.6 [3.0–4.1] vs. 4.8 [3.4–7.3] kg, p < 0.001). mBTTS procedures had higher rates of ventricular dysfunction (34.3% vs. 12.7%, p < 0.001), chromosomal abnormalities (63.9% vs. 19.1%, p < 0.001), gastrointestinal comorbidities (87.5% vs. 72.1%, p = 0.014), and hematologic comorbidities (41.7% vs. 22.8%, p = 0.006). Hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive support was the most common perioperative complication and occurred similarly between groups (31.9% mBTTS vs. 31.6% Sano, p = 0.962). There were no perioperative cardiac arrests. Rates of postoperative escalation of care (2.9%), reintubation (3.0% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999), readmission (16.2% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.999), and 30‐day mortality (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999) were low and comparable between groups. Conclusions Despite the high‐risk physiology of interstage SV patients, perioperative outcomes were comparable between Sano and mBTTS cohorts. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not imply low procedural risk. Favorable outcomes likely reflect careful patient selection, multidisciplinary perioperative care, and specialized institutional expertise.

papers.abstract: The erector spinae plane block (ESPB) is widely used for primary breast cancer surgery (BCS), though its clinical benefits within optimized multimodal analgesia pathways remain uncertain. Intravenous lidocaine infusion (IVLI) offers a simple, reproducible alternative with potential systemic analgesic effects. This randomized, tripleblinded, placebo controlled, twocentre trial compared the quality of recovery after ESPB versus IVLI for BCS. Eighty adult patients undergoing primary BCS, with or without axillary dissection, were randomized to receive either ultrasoundguided ESPB (n=40) or intraoperative IVLI (n=40), in addition to a standardized multimodal analgesic protocol. The primary outcome was quality of recovery (QoR15) score at 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, adverse events, and rescue analgesia requirements. Both interventions produced excellent postoperative recovery, with 24hour QoR15 scores approaching preoperative baselines with no significant difference between groups (mean (SD) 24-hour QoR score; ESPB vs. IVLI group, 137.7(17.9) vs. 136.3(8.8), p=0.61). Pain burden and analgesic requirements over the first 24 hours were similarly low, and no ESPB or lidocainerelated adverse events were observed. Within a standardized multimodal analgesic framework, postoperative recovery and analgesic outcomes did not differ significantly between IVLI and ESPB, suggesting that IVLI may offer a pragmatic alternative when regional anesthesia expertise is limited.

papers.abstract: Recovery after non-cardiac surgery increasingly occurs at home, where clinical deterioration may go unrecognized. Digital health interventions may extend postoperative surveillance beyond discharge, but vary widely in components and clinician involvement. We evaluated their association with readmission and other outcomes. Five databases were searched from inception to December 12, 2025, for prospective randomized and observational studies comparing digital health interventions with standard care in adults after non-cardiac surgery. Readmission was the primary outcome; all-cause and major complications, emergency room (ER) visits, length of stay (LOS), and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were secondary. Interventions were grouped by whether a clinician reviewed patient-submitted data and had the ability to take action (active clinician involvement). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and standardized mean differences (SMD). p values were adjusted for multiple comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg). In 38 studies (30 randomized, 8 observational; 7,494 patients), digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions (17 studies, n=3,944; RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.99, adjusted p=0.045), ER visits (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.97), and major complications (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.94), but not all-cause complications (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79-1.08) or LOS (MD -0.04 days, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.18). Pain and anxiety were lower and functional status, quality-of-life, and satisfaction scores higher (absolute SMD 0.41-0.69). Readmission risk was lower with active clinician involvement (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.92) but not without it (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78-1.18; interaction p=0.029). Heterogeneity in interventions, cohorts, and outcomes was substantial (PROM I² 50-97%). Digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions, ER visits, major complications, and better PROMs, but not fewer all-cause complications or shorter LOS. The readmission association was concentrated in studies with active clinician involvement. Heterogeneity was substantial and certainty of evidence low to very low.

papers.abstract: Paratracheal air cysts are rare benign anatomical variants. Although case reports suggest that paratracheal air cysts may lead to complications such as difficult ventilation and pneumothorax in patients whose lungs are mechanically ventilated, their association with postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) remains unclear. We hypothesized that the presence of cysts is associated with an increased incidence of PPCs. In the context of COVID-19, we conducted a retrospective study of all patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia in 2020. On the basis of the presence of paratracheal air cysts, we divided patients into two groups: the paratracheal air cyst group and the paratracheal-air-cyst‑free group. The primary outcome was the incidence of PPCs. We used propensity score matching to adjust for confounding and performed multivariable logistic regression analysis in the matched cohort to assess the association. Among 7,208 patients, the prevalence of paratracheal air cysts was 2.0% (141/7,208). The incidence of PPCs was 22% (31/141) in the paratracheal air cyst group and 15% (43/280) in the paratracheal-air-cyst-free group. Multivariable regression analysis showed that, after adjusting for confounders, the presence of paratracheal air cysts was associated with an increased risk of PPCs (adjusted odds ratio, 1.85; 95% confidence interval, 1.03 to 3.33; P = 0.04). The presence of paratracheal air cysts was associated with an increased risk of PPCs. Although this association warrants cautious interpretation due to possible residual confounding and lack of data on intraoperative ventilatory settings, anesthesiologists should consider the potential perioperative implications of this anatomical abnormality during preoperative assessment.

papers.abstract: Given the fiduciary responsibility of an academic clinical department to ensure appropriate use of funds to support research, the Department of Anesthesia, Pain Management and Perioperative Medicine at Dalhousie University (Halifax, NS, Canada) aimed to create a framework to support the allocation of remunerated protected research time to clinician faculty members within the department. A departmental Research Accountability Project (RAP) was undertaken in the context of a quality improvement initiative. The RAP initially engaged clinician faculty members in the form of a survey, interviews, and a questionnaire to provide feedback regarding current practices for evaluating protected time for research. On the basis of this feedback, a working group created a list of 151 research outputs encompassing the breadth of research-related activities and assigned scores based on their relative merit. Clinicians with protected research time completed their academic profile, and individual point allocations were calculated. Scores were then weighted by different categories (e.g., publications, grant capture, presentations), and a RAP dashboard was developed to capture research outputs, assign scores, and generate a reporting/feedback mechanism for further analysis. Faculty members acknowledged the importance of clinicians having remunerated protected time to carry out research; nevertheless, there was scepticism with respect to how protected research time was managed. These data were then assessed by the working group, and using the RAP metric, individual researcher reports consisting of scores and recommendations were sent to the department head for final evaluation. These reports formed the basis of the researchers' annual academic performance review and consideration for continuance. The RAP scoring system provides an objective measure of remunerated protected research time for clinicians to assist in researcher accountability.

papers.abstract: Predicting difficult intubation is still challenging, even with videolaryngoscopy. Videolaryngoscopy (VL) shows the larynx during intubation. The modified Cormack-Lehane (CL) classification grades laryngeal visibility but can vary between observers. Deep learning uses neural networks for objective, real-time airway image evaluation. We aimed to evaluate a YOLOv8-based model for object detection to automate modified CL grade classification from VL images in patients undergoing elective surgery. In this prospective observational study, we developed a deep learning model using 346 VL images from 151 patients undergoing elective surgery. Two anesthesiologists classified images according to the modified CL system, and interobserver agreement was analysed using Cohen's kappa and weighted kappa. We split the data into training (80%), validation (10%), and test (10%) sets, with imbalance corrected via Albumentations augmentation. We evaluated the model results using sensitivity, specificity, and mean average precision with a 95% confidence interval (CI) and validated the model on 60 images not included in the training set. Interobserver agreement ranged from moderate (Cohen's kappa = 0.59; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.66) to good (weighted kappa = 0.79; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.84). In the test set, the overall recall rate was 0.87, and the specificity was 0.83. In the difficult intubation grades, recall and specificity were observed to be 0.79 (95% CI, 0.52 to 0.92) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.98), respectively, for CL grade 2b, and 0.60 and 1.00, respectively, for CL grade 3. In the external validation data set (n = 60), the model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.767 with a recognition rate of 0.925 for clinically relevant CL grades 2b and 3. The YOLOv8-based model showed promising performance in classifying modified CL grades, particularly for clinically relevant difficult views (CL grades 2b-3). Nevertheless, wide CIs and limited external validation indicate uncertainty. The model may be considered an auxiliary tool rather than an independent decision system and requires further validation in larger, multicentre data sets.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Difficult tracheal intubation is associated with serious complications, including hypoxia, bradycardia and cardiac arrest. Neonates have increased physiologic vulnerability compared with older children, yet detailed data on management strategies and outcomes in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation remain limited. We hypothesised that clinicians have lower first‐attempt tracheal intubation success and higher complication rates for neonates compared with older children with difficult tracheal intubation. Methods We analysed the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry to determine tracheal intubation first attempt success and incidence of complications. We used logistic regression to identify variables associated with complications in neonates. Results During the study period, 6283 paediatric difficult tracheal intubations were recorded, including 420 neonates. First attempt success was lower for neonates (139/420, 33.1%) than older children (2394/4683, 51.1%). Complications occurred more frequently in neonates (123/420, 29.3%) than older children (637/4683, 13.6%). Hypoxia occurred in 92/420 (21.9%) neonates and 269/4683 (5.7%) older children. Severe complications were more frequent in neonates vs. older children (12/420, 2.9% vs. 30/4683, 0.6%, respectively), with cardiac arrests occurring in 4/420 (1.0%) neonates and 11/4683 (0.2%) older children. Difficult mask ventilation occurred more frequently in neonates (60/420, 14.3%) than older children (353/4681, 7.5%). In neonates, increased number of tracheal intubation attempts (aOR 1.61 per attempt, 95%CI 1.30–2.00, p < 0.001) and difficult facemask ventilation (aOR 3.17, 95%CI 1.38–7.30, p = 0.007) were associated with complications. Anticipated difficulty with airway management had a protective effect (aOR 0.37, 95%CI 0.16–0.88, p = 0.025). Discussion Neonates with difficult tracheal intubation experience a substantially higher rate of complications than older children. Early recognition of risk is critical in order to enable careful planning to minimise tracheal intubation attempts in this vulnerable population.

papers.abstract: Heart rate (HR) and arterial blood pressure (BP) monitoring is standard of care during paediatric anaesthesia, yet evidence-based reference values for anaesthetised children remain limited. Existing BP reference values do not account for the combined effects of age, sex, weight, and height, and HR reference values in this population are lacking. We conducted a retrospective multicentre study using data from the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group anaesthesia registry (2016-22). Included patients were aged <18 yr, ASA physical status 1 or 2, and undergoing noncardiac procedures under general anaesthesia. We used quantile regression to model the 2.3rd, 16th, 50th, 84th, and 97.7th centiles for HR, mean arterial pressure (MAP), systolic BP, and diastolic BP at two time points: the preparation phase (end of induction) and surgical phase (15-35 min after procedure start). Model covariates included age, sex, weight, and height. We selected the best model for each outcome using cross-validation with pinball loss. A total of 284 385 patients from 57 institutions were analysed. Optimal model complexity varied by outcome: a two-way interaction model was selected as the best-performing model for preparation phase HR and surgical phase MAP. A three-way interaction model was selected as the best-performing model for the remaining outcomes. Comprehensive prediction tables and an interactive web-based tool were developed for all outcomes. This study provides integrated HR and BP reference values for healthy paediatric patients undergoing general anaesthesia, incorporating age, sex, weight, and height simultaneously. These reference values with an interactive website can support clinical decision-making and haemodynamic monitoring.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Videolaryngoscopy has been associated with improved glottic visualisation and higher first‐attempt tracheal intubation success compared with direct laryngoscopy. However, multicentre evidence evaluating its effectiveness when tracheal intubation is performed by anaesthesia resident doctors in routine practice is limited. Methods Adult patients undergoing surgery requiring tracheal intubation were assigned to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy for the initial attempt. All tracheal intubations were performed by anaesthesia residents under consultant supervision. The primary outcome was successful tracheal intubation on the first attempt. Secondary outcomes included glottic visualisation; number of tracheal intubation attempts; need for adjunct airway devices; procedural difficulty; and procedural complications. Results We enrolled 1001 patients and assigned 501 to videolaryngoscopy and 500 patients to direct laryngoscopy. Successful first‐attempt tracheal intubation was achieved in 397 (79.2%) patients allocated to the videolaryngoscopy group and 351 (70.2%) patients allocated to the direct laryngoscopy group (absolute risk difference 9.0%, 95%CI 3.7–14.4%, p < 0.001). Videolaryngoscopy improved glottic visualisation, with more patients having a modified Cormack–Lehane grade 2 or 2a view (467/501 (93.3%) vs. 404/500 (80.8%); p < 0.001); decreased operator‐reported tracheal intubation difficulty (168/501 (33.5%) vs. 236/500 (47.2%); p < 0.001) and reduced procedural complications (39/501 (7.7%) vs. 91/500 (18.2%); p < 0.001), without a clinically meaningful difference in tracheal intubation time or the need for adjunct airway devices. Discussion In adult patients undergoing tracheal intubation by anaesthesia resident doctors, videolaryngoscopy increased first‐attempt success and improved overall procedural performance compared with direct laryngoscopy.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Intraoperative hypotension is a common complication in pediatric anesthesia. The definition of hypotension and treatment strategies are heterogeneous. The association of these treatments with cerebral regional oxygen saturation, measured by near‐infrared spectroscopy, is insufficiently characterized. Aims The study explores whether changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate differ after the administration of an isotonic fluid bolus, noradrenaline, adrenaline, or cafedrine/theodrenaline for perioperative hypotension in children. Methods This single‐center, observational pilot study included children aged 18 years or younger undergoing noncardiac surgery who developed hypotension requiring treatment. The choice of the intervention was at the discretion of the attending anesthetist and guided by an internal guideline. Cerebral regional oxygen saturation, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate were recorded for 8 min after the first intervention and analyzed relative to the value immediately before treatment. Groups were compared using the area under the curve of these changes and linear mixed‐effects models. Results Forty‐six patients were analyzed. Cerebral regional oxygen saturation immediately before treatment did not differ from the pre‐induction baseline. Cafedrine/theodrenaline was the only treatment associated with a sustained increase in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, with a significantly higher area under the curve than noradrenaline ( p = 0.017), adrenaline ( p = 0.017), and fluid administration ( p < 0.001), which was confirmed by mixed‐effects models. Only cafedrine/theodrenaline was associated with an increase in heart rate. Changes in heart rate were significantly correlated with changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation (Spearman's ρ = 0.376, p = 0.010), but not with changes in mean arterial pressure. Conclusions Cafedrine/theodrenaline was associated with a sustained increase in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, heart rate, and blood pressure. Noradrenaline, adrenaline, and fluid administration were associated with unchanged or decreasing cerebral regional oxygen saturation. Randomized controlled studies are required to confirm these findings.
